topic: Article 124 in the Constitution of India
subject: Polity & Governance
question_text:
Consider the following statements 
regarding Article 124 of the Constitution of 
India: 
 
1. A person who has served as a Judge of two or 
more High Courts in succession for an aggregate 
period of five years is eligible for appointment 
as a Judge of the Supreme Court. 
2. A person who has been an advocate of two or 
more High Courts in succession for ten years is 
eligible for appointment as a Judge of the 
Supreme Court. 
3. The Constitution mandates that at least one 
distinguished jurist must be appointed to the 
Supreme Court. 
 
Which of the statements given above is/are 
correct?
explanation:
In NEWS: Supreme Court Gets Five New Judges 
as President Approves Appointments 
 
Article 124 in Constitution of India - 
Establishment and Constitution of Supreme 
Court 
 
(1) There shall be a Supreme Court of India 
consisting of a Chief Justice of India  and, until 
Parliament by law prescribes a larger number, 
of not more than seven other Judges. 
(2) Every Judge of the Supreme Court shall be 
appointed by the President by warrant under 
his hand and seal  on the recommendation of 
the National Judicial Appointments 
Commission referred to in article 124A and 
shall hold office until he attains the age of sixty -
five years: 
Provided that-- 
(a) a Judge may, by writing under his hand 
addressed to the President, resign his office 
(b) a Judge may be removed from his office in 
the manner provided in clause (4). 
 
(2A) The age of a Judge of the Supreme Court  
shall be determined by such authority and in 
such manner as Parliament may by law 
provide. 
[Editorial comment-The Constitution (Fifteenth 
Amendment) Act, 1963 , in Article 124, a new 
clause (2A) was added. The age requirement for 
serving as a judge on the Supreme Court will be 
set by such power and in such way as 
Parliament may by legislation prescribe.] 
 
(3) A person shall not be qualified for 
appointment as a Judge of the Supreme Court  
unless he is a citizen of India and-- 
(a) has been for at least five years  a Judge of a 
High Court or of two or more such Courts in 
succession; or Hence statement 1 is correct. 
(b) has been for at least ten years an advocate 
of a High Court or of two or more such  courts in 
succession; or Hence statement 2 is correct. 
(c) is, in the opinion of the President, a 
distinguished jurist. 
●  The Constitution merely permits the 
appointment of a distinguished jurist as a 
Supreme Court Judge. It does not require  that 
any seat be re served for a distinguished jurist,  
nor does it mandate that at least one such 
person be appointed. Hence statement 3 is 
incorrect. 
 
Explanation I-- this clause "High Court' means a 
High Court which exercises, or which at any 
time before the commencement of  this 
Constitution exercised, jurisdiction in any part 
of the territory of India. 
Explanation II--In computing for the purpose of 
this clause the period during which a person has 
been an advocate, any period during which a 
person has held judicial office n ot inferior to 
that of a district Judge after he became an 
advocate shall be included. 
 
(4) A Judge of the Supreme Court shall not be 
removed from his office except by an order of 
the President passed after an address by each 
House of Parliament supported b y a majority of 
the total membership of that House and by a 
majority of not less than two -third of the 
members of the House present and voting  
has been presented to the President in the same 
session for such removal on the ground of 
proved misbehavior or incapacity. 
 
(5) Parliament may by law regulate the 
procedure for the presentation of an address 
and for the investigation and proof of the  
misbehavior or incapacity  of a Judge under 
clause (4): 
 
(6) Every person appointed to be a Judge of the 
Supreme Court  shall, before he enters upon his 
office, make and subscribe before the President, 
or some person appointed in that behalf by him, 
an oath or affirmation according to the form set 
out for the purpose in the Third Schedule. 
 
(7) No person who has held offic e as a Judge of 
the Supreme Court shall plead or act in any 
court or before any authority within the 
territory of India.
in_news: Supreme Court Gets Five New Judges as President Approves Appointments

subject: Polity & Governance
question_text:
Consider the following statements with 
reference to the Special Intensive Revision 
(SIR) of Electoral Rolls: 
 
1. There is no provision in the Constitution that 
explicitly uses the term "Special Intensive 
Revision". 
2. There is no Article in the Constitution that 
specifically prescribes the procedure for house -
to-house verification of electors. 
3. There i s no Article in the Constitution that 
expressly empowers the Election Commission to 
prepare and revise electoral rolls. 
 
Which one of the following conclusions 
based on the above statements is correct?
option_c: There are two correct statements that include statement 2.
option_d: There is only one correct statement.
explanation:
statements that include statement 2. 
 
Explanation:  
In NEWS:  Enumeration Phase has started for 
the states of Odis ha, Mizoram, Sikkim and 
Manipur 
 
Special Intensive Revision (SIR) 
 Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is a 
comprehensive revision of electoral rolls 
conducted by the Election Commission of 
India (ECI). 
 It involves house -to-house verification of 
voters through Booth Level Officers (BLOs). 
 Electoral rolls are prepared and revised 
under the Representation of the People Act, 
1950 
 
Constitutional and Legal Basis 
 The Election Commission of India, in exercise 
of its powers under Article 324 of the 
Constitution of Ind ia; Hence statement 3 is 
incorrect. 
 Section 21 along with other applicable 
provisions of the Representation of the People 
Act, 1950, has ordered Special Intensive 
Revision (SIR) in 16 States and 3 Union 
Territories (UTs) on May 14, 2026. 
 The main objective  of the Special Intensive 
Revision (SIR) is -  
○ No eligible citizen is left out while no 
ineligible person is included in the Electoral 
Roll.  
○ Every person who is a citizen of India and 
who is not less than eighteen years of age on 
the qualifying date and is not otherwise 
disqualified under any law shall be entitled to 
be registered in the electoral roll.
value_addition:
 The term Special Intensive Revision (SIR) 
does not appear in the Constitution. Hence 
statement 1 is correct. 
 The Constitution does not prescribe 
operational procedures such as house -to-house 
verification; these are governed by electoral 
laws and ECI instructions. Hence statement 2 
is correct.

subject: History & Culture
question_text:
With reference to the life of Shakyamuni 
Buddha, consider the following events: 
 
1. Enlightenment at Bodh Gaya 
2. Birth at Lumbini 
3. First Sermon at Sarnath 
4. Mahaparinirvana at Kushinagar 
 
Arrange the above events in the correct 
chronological order:
explanation:
In NEWS: Sacred Relics of Lord Buddha's Chief 
Disciples Enshrined in Mongolia - Exhibition 
"Vessels of Light" Opens at Gandantegchenling 
Monastery 
 Sacred relics of Arhat Sariputra and Arhat 
Mahamoggallana, the two chief disciples of 
Gautama Buddha, we re ceremonially enshrined 
at Gandantegchenling Monastery. 
 A special exhibition titled "Vessels of Light: 
Iconography, Relics and Path of Dhamma - 
Shakyamuni Buddha's Journey  through 
Museum Collections of India" was also 
inaugurated on the premises of 
Gandantegchenling Monastery. 
 
 
Path of Dhamma - Shakyamuni Buddha's 
Journey 
 
 
 
 
Shakyamuni Buddha , born as Siddhartha 
Gautama, was a prince of the Shakya clan who 
renounced worldly life in search of the truth 
behind human suffering. After witnessing old 
age, disease, and death, he left his palace and 
began a spiritual quest known as the Path of 
Dhamma. 
 
Major Stages of the Journey 
1. Birth at Lumbini 
○ Siddhartha was born at Lumbini in present -
day Nepal to Queen Maya and King Suddhodana. 
2. The Four Sights 
○ He encountered an old man, a sick person, a 
dead body, and an ascetic. 
○ These experiences revealed the realities of 
life and inspired him to seek liberation from 
suffering. 
3. The Great Departure 
○ At the age of 29, he renounced his royal life 
and left Kapilavastu in search of enlightenment. 
4. Years of Asceticism 
○ He practiced severe austerities for about six 
years but realized that extreme self -denial could 
not lead to liberation. 

 
5. Enlightenment at Bodh Gaya 
○ Meditating under the Bodhi Tree, Siddhartha 
attained enlightenment at  the age of 35 and 
became the Buddha, meaning "The Enlightened 
One." 
6. First Sermon at Sarnath 
○ Buddha delivered his first sermon at Deer 
Park, Sarnath. 
○ He explained the Four Noble Truths and the 
Noble Eightfold Path , setting in motion the 
"Wheel of Dhamma." 
7. Spread of Dhamma 
○ For about 45 years, Buddha travelled across 
northern India teaching compassion, non -
violence, mindfulness, and the Middle Path. 
8. Mahaparinirvana 
○ At Kushinagar, Buddha attained 
Mahaparinirvana, marking the end of his earthly 
life. 
 
Core Teachings of Dhamma 
 Four Noble Truths 
 Noble Eightfold Path 
 Middle Path 
 Compassion and Non-violence 
 Impermanence (Anicca) 
 Non-self (Anatta) 
The journey of Shakyamuni Buddha represents 
humanity's quest to overcome suffering through 
wisdom, ethical conduct, and m ental discipline, 
forming the foundation of Buddhism.
in_news: Sacred Relics of Lord Buddha's Chief Disciples Enshrined in Mongolia - Exhibition

subject: Environment & Ecology
question_text:
With respect to Babesiosis, which of the 
following statements is/are correct? 
 
1. It is a tick -borne disease caused by 
protozoan parasites of the genus Babesia. 
2. The disease spreads directly from one 
infected lion to another through physical 
contact. 
3. It destroys red blood cells and can cause 
severe illness in infected animals. 
 
Select t he answer using the code given 
below:
explanation:
In NEWS: Eight dead, 17 on the way to recovery 
as tick infection spreads among world's only 
Asiatic lion population 
 
Babesiosis Outbreak in Asiatic Lions 
 Babesiosis is a tick -borne disease caused by 
protozoan parasites of the genus Babesia. 
Hence statement 1 is correct. 
 The disease destroys red blood cells, causing 
anemia, weakness, fever, coughing and 
respiratory compli cations. Hence statement 3 
is correct. 
 Babesiosis is a vector-borne disease  and 
does not spread directly from one animal to 
another. Hence statement 2 is incorrect. 
 Ticks associated with domestic livestock are 
considered a major source of transmission. 
 In 2026, 8 Asiatic lions died  and 17 lions 
were infected in the Gir landscape of Gujarat. 
 
 The world's only wild population of Asiatic 
Lions ( Panthera leo persica ) is found in 
Gujarat. 
 According to the 2025 census, Gujarat has 
891 Asiatic lions. 
 Asiatic Lion i s classified as Endangered by 
the IUCN. 
 Major protected areas for Asiatic lions 
include Gir National Park , Gir Wildlife 
Sanctuary, Pania Wildlife Sanctuary , and 
Barda Wildlife Sanctuary. 
 In 2018, an outbreak of Canine Distemper 
Virus (CDV) caused the death  of several Asiatic 
lions in Gir. 
 The combination of Babesiosis and Canine 
Distemper Virus can significantly increase lion 
mortality. 
 A single concentrated population makes 
Asiatic lions vulnerable to disease outbreaks, 
natural disasters and other extinction risks. 
 In 2013, the Supreme Court directed the 
translocation of Asiatic lions from Gir to Kuno 
National Park  to establish a second free -
ranging population. 
 Kuno National Park is located in Madhya 
Pradesh and was identified as the second home 
for Asiatic lions. 
 Establishing geographically separate 
populations is an important conservation 
strategy to reduce extinction risks. 
 Asiatic lions are listed in Schedule I of the 
Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.

question_text:
Ghepan Lake, recently seen in the new s, is 
located in:
explanation:
In NEWS: How big a threat is the expanding 
Ghepan Lake above Sissu village in Himachal 
Pradesh? 
 
Ghepan Lake: 
 Ghepan Lake  is a glacial lake located in the 
Lahaul-Spiti district  of Himachal Pradesh. 
Hence option (c) is correct. 
 It lies near Sissu village in the Chandra sub -
basin of the Indus River system. 
 The lake is situated at an altitude of about 
4,100 metres (13,500 feet). 
 
Formation 
 It is a moraine-dammed glacial lake  
formed by the melting of the Ghepan 
(Ghepang) Glacier. 
 Moraine dams are natural barriers made of 
rocks, sand, debris and ice deposited by glaciers. 
 
Recent Concerns 
 The lake has expanded significantly due to 
climate-change-induced glacier melting. 
 Its area increased from about 36.49 
hectares in 1989 to 101.30 hectares in 2022. 
 Scientists have warned of the possibility of a 
Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF).

subject: History & Culture
question_text:
Which of the following statements o n 
Chand Baori are correct? 
 
1. It is located in the state of Gujarat. 
2. It was built by King Chanda of the Nikumbha 
Dynasty during the 8th-9th century CE. 
3. It has been constructed in an upside -down 
pyramid-style. 
4. It is situated adjacent to the Harshat Mata 
Temple. 
 
Select the answer using the code given 
below:
explanation:
In NEWS: Chand Baori, a stepwell marvel of 
India 
Stepwells hold the promise of ancient water 
wisdom in today's climate-stressed age 
 
Chand Baori: 
 Chand Baori is a famous stepwell located at 
Abhaneri village in Rajasthan . Hence 
statement 1 is incorrect. 
 It was built by King Chanda of the 
Nikumbha Dynasty  during the 8th-9th 
century CE. Hence statement 2 is correct. 
 It is one of the oldest, deepest, and largest 
stepwells in India. 
 This stepwell has been constructed in an 
upside-down pyramid -style. Hence statement 
3 is correct. 
 The structure extends nearly 30 metres 
(about 100 feet) below ground level. 
 On three sides, it has 3500 steps cascading 
13 stories deep into a massive tank at the 
bottom. The fourth side has pillared corridors at 
many levels. 
 It was constructed primarily for water 
conservation and storage  in the arid region of 
Rajasthan. 
 The lower le vels remain significantly cooler 
than the surface during summer. 
 One side of the structure contains a multi -
storeyed pavilion with balconies, galleries, and 
carved jharokhas. 
 Chand Baori is situated adjacent to the 
Harshat Mata Temple .Hence statement 4 is 
correct. 
 Chand Baori is an outstanding example of 
traditional water-harvesting architecture. 
 It reflects the advanced understanding of 
water management in medieval India. 
 The structure functioned as a water 
reservoir, social gathering space, and resting 
place for travellers. 
 It demonstrates the integration of 
architecture, engineering, and environmental 
adaptation in a semi-arid region 
Some important Baolis: 
1. Rani ki Vav                 Gujarat 
2. Adalaj Stepwell     Gujarat 
3. Dada Harir Stepwell    Gujarat 
4. Agrasen ki Baoli     Delhi 
5. Rajon Ki Baoli                Delhi 
6. Gandhak Ki Baoli     Delhi 
7. Toorji Ka Jhalra     Rajasthan 
8. Panna Meena ka Kund   Rajasthan 
9. Neemrana Baori     Rajasthan 
10. Ugrasen ki Baoli     Delhi 
11. Lakkundi Stepwells   Karnataka 
12. Pushkarani of Hampi    Karnataka 
13. Mukhed Stepwell     Maharashtra

subject: Geography
question_text:
Identify the river on the basis of the 
following information: 
 
1. It is formed by the confluence of the Chandra 
and Bhaga rivers at Tandi in Himachal Pradesh. 
2. It is one of the six major rivers of the Indus 
River System and is classified as a Western 
River under the Indus Waters Treaty. 
3. It flows through India and Pakistan before 
joining the Indus River. 
 
Select the answer from the following:
explanation:
In NEWS: Chenab-Beas River -Link Project 
Approved in Himachal Pradesh 
 
Chenab-Beas Link Tunnel Project: 
 The Chenab-Beas Link Tunnel Project  was 
approved by the Central Government in May 
2026. The project is located in Himachal 
Pradesh. 
 It aims to divert surplus water from the 
Chenab basin to the Beas river system. 
 The project includes an 8.7-km tunnel  for 
inter-basin water transfer. 
 Phase I includes a 19-metre-high barrage  
on the Chandra River  near Koksar in Lahaul 
Valley. 
 The Chandra River joins the Bhaga River at 
Tandi to form the Chenab River. 
 The project will be implemented by NHPC. It 
is expected to facilitate nearly 4,000 MW  of 
additional hydropower generation. 
 
Indus River System 
 The major rivers of the Indus system are 
Indus, Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej. 
 The Chenab is one of the Western Rivers  
under the Indus Waters Treaty. 
 The Beas is a tributary of the Sutlej River. 
 The Beas originates from Beas Kund  near 
Rohtang Pass in Himachal Pradesh.
in_news: Chenab-Beas River -Link Project Approved in Himachal Pradesh

subject: Economy
question_text:
Which of the following statements with 
respect to PM SVANidhi scheme are correct? 
 
1. It is a Central Sector Scheme implemented by 
the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium 
Enterprises. 
2. It provides collateral -free working capital 
loans to street vendors. 
3. It provides an interest subsidy of 7% per 
annum on timely or early repayment of loans. 
4. Initially a sum of ₹50,000 is provided for a 
repayment tenure of 12 months. 
 
Select the answer using the code given 
below:
explanation:
In NEWS: PM SVANidhi scheme completes six 
years of implementation 
 
PM SVANidhi: 
 PM SVANidhi provides collateral-free 
working capital loans to street vendors. 
Hence statement 2 is correct. 
 The scheme is a Central Sector Scheme 
implemented by the Ministry of Housing and 
Urban Affairs. Hence statement 1 is 
incorrect. 
 The Central Government has officially 
extended the scheme's implementation timeline 
until March 31, 2030. 
 
Eligible Applicants: 
 Street vendors vending on or before 24 
March 2020. 
 Vendors possessing a Certificate of Vending 
(CoV). 
 Vendors holding an Identity Card issued by 
the Urban Local Body. 
 Vendors with a Provisional Certificate of 
Vending. 
 Vendors having a Letter of Recommendation 
(LoR) from the Urban Local Body or Town 
Vending Committee. 
 Vendors operating in urban, peri -urban, and 
adjoining rural areas under Urban Local Bodies. 
 
Loan Disbursement: 
 First Tranche:  Up to ₹15,000 for a 
repayment tenure of 12 months. Hence 
statement 4 is incorrect. 
 
 Second Tranche:  Up to ₹25,000 for a 
repayment tenure of 24 months, unlocked upon 
timely repayment of the first loan. 
 Third Tranche: Up to ₹50,000 for a 
repayment tenure of 36 months, unlocked after 
successfully repaying the second loan 
 The loans are repayable through monthly 
installments over the prescribed tenure. 
 
Incentives: 
 The scheme provides an interest subsidy of 
7% per annum on timely or early repayment 
of loans. Hence statement 3 is correct. 
 The interest subsidy is credited directly to 
the beneficiary's bank account on a quarterly 
basis. 
 To promote digital transactions, the scheme 
offers monthly cashback incentives. 
 Vendors carrying out at least 50 eligible 
digital t ransactions per month can receive a 
cashback of ₹50. 
 Vendors carrying out at least 100 eligible 
digital transactions per month can receive a 
cashback of ₹75. 
 Vendors carrying out 200 or more eligible 
digital transactions per month can receive a 
cashback of ₹100. 
 The maximum cashback available under the 
scheme is ₹100 per month or ₹1,200 per year. 
 Eligible street vendors who successfully 
repay their tranches can access a UPI -linked 
RuPay credit card with an initial operating limit 
of up to ₹30,000.
in_news: PM SVANidhi scheme completes six years of implementation

subject: General Studies
question_text:
Which one of the following Carnatic music 
ragas is similar to Raga Bilawal in 
Hindustani music?
explanation:
Dheera Shankarabharanam:  
 In Indian classical music, Raga Bilawal (or 
Bilawal Thaat) serves as the fundamental, 
standard scale of Hindustani music  where all 
seven notes are natural (Shuddha Swaras). 
Hence option (d) is correct. 
 In Carnatic music, the exact structural 
equivalent that employs the identical purely 
natural note interval structure is Dheera 
Shankarabharanam (the 29th Melakarta raga).  
 This specific scale corresponds musically to 
the standard Major Scale (C Major) in Western 
classical music. 
Nat Bhairavi: This is the 20th Melakarta raga in 
Carnatic music. It is the structural equivalent of 
the Asavari Thaat in Hindustani music , 
featuring flat (komal) intervals for the notes Ga, 
Dha, and Ni. 
 
Kamavardhini: Also widely known as 
Pantuvarali, this is the 51st Melakarta raga. 
Itcorresponds to the Poorvi Thaat in 
Hindustani music and is characterized by a 
raised sharp note (Prati Madhyama or Tivra 
Madhyam). 
 
Hanumatodi: This is the 8th Melakarta raga in 
the Carnatic system. It corresponds directly to 
the Bhairavi Thaat  of Hindustani music, 
consisting of all flat (komal) notes.

subject: General Studies
question_text:
Consider the following statements 
regarding index of industrial production  
  
1. Index of industrial production is released by 
the National Statistical Office (NSO)  
2. The base year has been revised to 2022 -
2023 
3. Mining and quarrying constitute the highest 
weight in newly revised item basket  
4. Water supply , sewerage and waste 
management has been newly added in the new 
IIP series  
 
 
How many  of the statements given abov e 
are correct?
explanation:
Statement 1: 
Index of Industrial Production is released by 
the National Statistical Office (NSO). 
The Index of Industrial Production (IIP) is 
compiled and released every month by the 
National Statistical Office (NSO)  under the 
Ministry of Statistics and Programme 
Implementation (MoSPI). It measures changes 
in the volume of production of industrial sectors 
such as mining, manufacturing and 
electricity.Hence, Statement 1 is correct. 
 
Statement 2: 
The base year has been revised to 2022-23. 
The Government has approved the revision of 
the IIP base year to 2022 -23 and the revised 
series has been introduced to better reflect the 
current structure of the  Indian economy and 
industrial production patterns. Hence, 
Statement 2 is correct. 
 
Statement 3: 
Mining and Quarrying constitute the highest 
weight in the newly revised item basket. In 
the revised IIP series (Base Year: 2022 -23), the 
Manufacturing sector con tinues to have the 
highest weight , followed by Electricity and 
Mining & Quarrying. Therefore, Mining and 
Quarrying do not constitute the highest 
weight.Hence, Statement 3 is incorrect. 
 
Statement 4: 
Water Supply, Sewerage and Waste 
Management has been newl y added in the 
new IIP series. The revised IIP series has 
expanded coverage by including Water Supply, 
Sewerage, Waste Management and 
Remediation Activities , aligning the index 
more closely with international industrial 
classification standards and capturin g a broader 
spectrum of economic activity. Hence, 
Statement 4 is correct. 
 
Additional Information 
Index of Industrial Production (IIP) 
 A composite indicator that measures the 
growth of industrial activity in India. 
 Released monthly by the National 
Statistical Office (NSO). 
 Serves as an important indicator of the 
performance of the industrial sector. 
 
Major Sectors Covered 
 Mining and Quarrying 
 Manufacturing 
 Electricity 
 Water Supply, Sewerage, Waste Management 
and Remediation Activities (newly added) 
 
Purpose of Base Year Revision 
 Reflect structural changes in the economy. 
 Incorporate new products and industries. 
 Improve data coverage and methodology. 
 Align with international statistical standards. 
IN NEWS:Industrial output slows to 4.9% in 
new data series

subject: International Relations
question_text:
Consider the following statements 
regarding BRICS: 
 
1. BRICS was originally formed by Brazil, 
Russia, India and China. 
2. South Africa joined BRICS in 2010. 
3. The New Development Bank was established 
by BRICS countries. 
4. All BRICS members are members of the G20. 
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
Statement 1: 
BRICS was originally formed by Brazil, Russia, 
India and China.The gr ouping was initially 
known as BRIC, comprising Brazil, Russia, India 
and China. The term BRIC was coined in 2001 
by economist Jim O'Neill. The first BRIC Summit 
was held in 2009 .Hence, Statement 1 is 
correct. 
 
Statement 2: 
South Africa joined BRICS in 2010 .South Africa 
was invited to join the grouping in 2010 and 
participated in its first BRICS Summit in 2011, 
after which the grouping became known as 
BRICS.Hence, Statement 2 is correct. 
 
Statement 3: 
The New Development Bank was established by 
BRICS countri es.The New Development Bank 
(NDB) was established by BRICS countries 
during the 6th BRICS Summit held in Fortaleza, 
Brazil, in 2014 to finance infrastructure and 
sustainable development projects in emerging 
and developing economies .Hence, Statement 3 
is correct. 
 
Statement 4: 
All BRICS members are members of the G20.Not 
all BRICS members are part of the G20. While 
Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Saudi 
Arabia and Indonesia are G20 members, 
countries such as Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the 
United Ar ab Emirates are not .Hence, 
Statement 4 is incorrect. 
 
Additional Information

India, China).

members.

○ Reform of Global Governance Institutions 
○ Economic and Development Cooperation

 Purpose: Infrastructure and Sustainable 
Development Financing 
 Founding Members: Brazi l, Russia, India, 
China and South Africa

question_text:
With reference to summer air pollution in 
Indian cities, consider the following 
statements: 
 
1. PM10 is a major air pollutant during summer 
and is often associated with dust storms and 
construction activities. 
2. Ground-level ozone is directly emitted from 
vehicles and industries. 
 
Which of the statements given above is/are 
correct?
explanation:
Statement 1: 
 During summer, air pollution is largely driven 
by PM10 (coarse particula te matter). Dust 
storms such as Loo and Andhi, along with 
construction and demolition activities, 
significantly increase PM10 levels.  Hence, 
Statement 1 is correct. 
 
Statement 2: 
 Ground-level ozone is not directly emitted. It is 
a secondary pollutant form ed when Nitrogen 
Oxides (NOx) and Volatile Organic Compounds 
(VOCs) react in the presence of sunlight.  Hence, 
Statement 2 is incorrect. 
Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs) are carbon -
based chemical compounds that easily 
 
evaporate into the atmosphere at norma l 
temperatures. 
 
Sources of VOCs 
●  Vehicle exhaust emissions 
●  Petroleum refineries and industries 
●  Paints, varnishes, solvents, and adhesives 
●  Fuel storage and distribution systems 
●  Biomass burning and waste burning 
 
Additional Information 
●  PM10:refers to particu late matter having an 
aerodynamic diameter of 10 micrometres or 
less. 
●  Major Summer Pollutants: PM10 and 
ground-level ozone. 
●  Ground-level Ozone Formation: NOx + VOCs 
+ Sunlight → Ozone. 
●  Health Impact: Causes respiratory illnesses 
and aggravates asthma and lung diseases. 
●  Key Sources of PM10: Dust storms, road dust, 
construction and demolition activities.

With reference to the National 
Investigation Agency (NIA), consider the

committed outside India, subject to 
international treaties and the domestic laws of 
other countries.

offences that can be investigated by the NIA. 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
1. The National Invest igation Agency (NIA) 
functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs 
(MHA), not under the Ministry of Personnel, 
Public Grievances and Pensions. The NIA was 
established under the National Investigation 
Agency Act, 2008 as a central counter -terrorism 
investigative agency. Hence, Statement 1 is 
incorrect. 
 
2. The National Investigation Agency 
(Amendment) Act, 2019  expanded the 
jurisdiction of the NIA by empowering it to 
investigate scheduled offences committed 
outside India , subject to international treaties 
and the domestic laws of the concerned country. 
The Central Government may direct the NIA to 
investigate such offences as if they had been 
committed in India  Hence, Statement 2 is 
correct. 
 
3. The NIA (Amendment) Act, 2019,  included 
several new offences in th e Schedule of the Act, 
including cyber-terrorism, human trafficking, 
 
offences related to counterfeit currency, 
manufacture or sale of prohibited arms, and 
offences under the Explosive Substances Act, 
1908. Hence, Statement 3 is correct.

anywhere in India without prior consent of the

Consider the following statements 
regarding the Forest Rights Act (FRA), 2006:

community rights of forest -dwelling Scheduled 
Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers.

for receiving, verifying and consolidating claims 
under the Act. 
3. Individual forest rights recognized under the 
Act are transferable and can be sold in the open 
market. 
4. No member of a forest -dwelling community 
can be evicted from forest land under 
occupation until the recognition and verification 
process is complete. 
 
How many of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
Statement 1: The Forest Rights Act, 2006, 
recognizes both Individual Forest Rights (IFR) 
and Community F orest Rights (CFR) for 
Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest 
Dwellers. Hence, Statement 1 is correct. 
 
Statement 2: The Gram Sabha is the nodal 
authority at the village level. It receives, verifies 
and consolidates claims and forwards its 
recommendations to higher committees.  Hence, 
Statement 2 is correct. 
 
Statement 3: Titles granted under the FRA are 
heritable but not transferable. They cannot be 
sold or transferred in the open market.  Hence, 
Statement 3 is incorrect. 
 
Statement 4: Section 4(5) of  the FRA protects 
against eviction and states that no eligible forest 
dweller shall be evicted until the process of 
recognition and verification of rights is 
completed. Hence, Statement 4 is correct.

subject: Environment & Ecology
question_text:
With reference to the recent tiger 
translocation efforts in Odisha, consider the 
following statements: 
 
1. Similipal Tiger Reserve is the only tiger 
reserve in India known for its population of 
melanistic (black) tigers. 
2. The National Tiger Conservation Authority 
(NTCA) facilitates the translocation of tigers 
between reserves to improve genetic diversity. 
3. The All India Tiger Estimation, conducted 
under the supervision of the National Tiger 
Conservation Authority (NTCA), is carried out 
every five years. 
 
Which of the statements given above is/are 
correct?
explanation:
1. Melanistic Tigers of Similipal: Similipal 
Tiger Reserve in Odisha is globally known for its 
unique population of melanistic (pseudo -
melanistic) tigers. These tigers are not a 
separate subspecies; rather, they exhibit a rare 
genetic mutation that results in unusually broad 
and merged stripes, giving them a black 
appearance. Similipal is the only tiger reserve in 
India where such a population occurs in the 
wild. Hence, Statement 1 is correct. 
 

 
2. Tiger Translocation and Genetic 
Diversity: The recent translocation of tigress 
Zeenat from Maharashtra to Similipal is part of a 
broader conservation strategy to improve 
genetic diversity. Isolated tiger populations are 
vulnerable to inbreeding, w hich can reduce 
fitness and adaptability. The NTCA, in 
collaboration with State Forest Departments, 
facilitates scientifically planned translocations 
to strengthen gene flow and improve the long -
term viability of tiger populations.  Hence, 
Statement 2 is correct. 
 
3. Frequency of Tiger Census: The All India 
Tiger Estimation (commonly called the tiger 
census) is conducted once every four years, not 
every five years. It is coordinated by the NTCA 
in association with the Wildlife Institute of India 
and State Fores t Departments. The exercise is 
regarded as one of the largest wildlife 
monitoring programmes in the world and uses 
methods such as camera trapping, sign surveys, 
and statistical modelling to estimate tiger 
populations. Hence, Statement 3 is incorrect. 
●  NTCA was established in 2005 following the 
Tiger Task Force recommendations, but it was 
statutorily constituted in 2006 through the 
Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2006.

question_text:
With reference to the impact of aircraft 
noise on human health, consider the 
following statements: 
 
1. Chronic exposure to aircraft noise may affect 
cardiovascular health even in the absence of 
hearing loss. 
2. The health effects of noise depend only on its 
loudness and not on the duration or frequency 
of exposure. 
3. Night-time aircraft noise is considered more 
harmful because it can disrupt sleep and 
recovery. 
 
Which of the statements given above is/are 
correct?
explanation:
1. Health Effects Beyond Hearing Loss 
Recent studies indicate that chronic aircraft 
noise can trigger stress -related biological 
responses, inflammation, oxidative stress, and 
cardiovascular effects ev en when conventional 
hearing tests show no hearing impairment. 
Thus, noise pollution can affect multiple 
physiological systems beyond the auditory 
system. Hence, Statement 1 is correct. 
 
2. Determinants of Noise -Related Health 
Risks 
The health impacts of n oise are influenced not 
only by its loudness but also by factors such as 
frequency of occurrence, duration of exposure, 
peak intensity, timing of exposure, and 
cumulative long -term effects. Adequate 
recovery periods between exposures, especially 
during sle ep, are also important. Hence, 
Statement 2 is incorrect. 
 
3, Importance of Night-time Recovery 
Night-time noise can disrupt sleep cycles and 
prevent adequate physiological recovery from

A bolide is an exceptionally bright meteor 
(often called a fireball) that enters the Earth's 
atmosphere at very high speed and may explode

produce intense flashes of light, shock waves, 
and sonic booms. Hence, option (b) is correct.

the asteroid belt , not a rocky planet. Hence, 
option (d) is incorrect.

in space.

subject: Economy
question_text:
With reference to inflation measurement 
in India, consider the following statements: 
 
1. The Producer Price Index (PPI) measures 
price changes from the perspective of producers 
and includes both input and output prices. 

 
2. Unlike the Wholesale Price Index (WPI), the 
Producer Price Index will also include services. 
3. The Wholesale Price Index (WPI) is compiled 
and released by the Reserve Bank of India. 
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
1. Producer-Centric Inflation Measure 
The Producer Price Index (PPI) measures 
changes in prices received by producers for 
their output as well as prices paid for inputs 
used in production. It provi des a more 
comprehensive picture of inflationary pressures 
across the production process.  Hence, 
Statement 1 is correct. 
 
Input Cost 
Input costs are the prices that producers pay for 
the goods and services used in the production 
process. 
Examples: 
●  A steel manufacturer is purchasing iron ore, 
coal, and electricity. 
●  A bakery purchases flour, sugar, and cooking 
gas. 
●  A textile mill purchases cotton and dyes. 
If the prices of these inputs rise, the producer's 
cost of production increases. 
Output Cost (Price Received by Producer) 
Output cost (more accurately, output price) 
refers to the price at which producers sell their 
finished goods or services. 
Examples: 
●  The price at which a steel company sells steel 
sheets. 
●  The price at which a bakery sells bread to 
wholesalers. 
●  The price charged by an airline for passenger 
transport services. 
 
2. Inclusion of Services 
The new PPI series proposed by the government 
includes not only goods but also the Services 
PPI. In the first phase, services such as banking, 
insurance, railw ays, air passenger transport, 
telecom, securities transactions, and pension 
fund management are included.  Hence, 
Statement 2 is correct. 
 
3. Compilation of WPI 
The Wholesale Price Index (WPI) is compiled 
and released by the Office of the Economic 
Adviser, Department for Promotion of 
Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), 
Ministry of Commerce and Industry , and not 
by the Reserve Bank of India. Hence, Statement 
3 is incorrect.

question_text:
Consider the following pairs of clouds and 
their characteristics: 
 
Cloud Type Characteristic 
1. Cumulus Cotton-ball shaped clouds 
formed due to convection 
2. Cirrostratus Halo effect around the Sun or 
Moon 
3. Altocumulus Indicates moisture and  
possible thunderstorm 
development 
4. Nimbostratus Produces continuous rainfall 
over long durations 
 
How many of the above pairs are correctly 
matched?
explanation:
Explanation 
1. Cumulus - Cotton-ball shaped clouds 
formed due to convection 
Cumulus clouds have flat bases and rounded 
tops, resembling cotton balls. They form due to 
the upward convection of warm air and 
generally indicate fair weather, though they may 
develop into storm clouds un der unstable 
conditions. Hence, Pair 1 is correctly 
matched. 
 
2. Cirrostratus - Halo effect around the Sun 
or Moon 
Cirrostratus clouds are thin, high -altitude 
clouds composed of ice crystals. They often 
produce halo effects around the Sun or Moon 
due to re fraction of light.  Hence, Pair 2 is 
correctly matched. 
 
3. Altocumulus - Indicates moisture and 
possible thunderstorm development 
Altocumulus clouds are middle -level clouds that 
indicate atmospheric moisture and instability. 
They may signal the development  of 
thunderstorms later in the day. Hence, Pair 3 is 
correctly matched. 
 
4. Nimbostratus - Produces continuous 
rainfall over long durations 
Nimbostratus clouds are thick, dark, layered 
clouds associated with steady and prolonged 
precipitation, such as rain  or snow. Hence, Pair 
4 is correctly matched. 
 
 
 
Value Addition 
🔹 Cumulus → Convection → Fair Weather 
🔹 Cumulonimbus → Thunderstorm, Lightning, 
Hail 
🔹 Cirrus → Weather Change Indicator 
🔹 Cirrostratus → Halo Formation 
🔹 Nimbostratus → Continuous Rainfall

question_text:
With reference to Electric Vehicles (EVs), 
consider the following statements: 
 
1. Lithium is a critical mineral used in EV 
batteries. 
2. Cobalt is used in some EV battery 
chemistries. 
3. Electric Vehicles do not em it tailpipe 
pollutants during operation. 
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
Statement 1: 
Lithium is one of the most important critical 
minerals used in lithium -ion batteries that 
power most Electric Vehicles. It helps in storing 
and releasing electrical energy efficiently. 
Hence, Statement 1 is correct. 
 
Statement 2: 
Cobalt is used in several lithium -ion battery 
chemistries to improve batte ry stability, safety, 
and energy density. It is considered a strategic 
mineral for the EV industry. Hence, Statement 
2 is correct. 
 
Statement 3: 
Electric Vehicles, particularly Battery Electric 
Vehicles (BEVs), run entirely on electricity and 
do not use an  internal combustion engine. 
Therefore, they do not emit exhaust gases or 
pollutants from a tailpipe during operation, 
helping reduce urban air pollution. Hence, 
Statement 3 is correct. 
 
Additional information: 
Types of EVs 
●  BEV (Battery Electric Vehicle): Runs entirely 
on electricity stored in batteries. 
●  HEV (Hybrid Electric Vehicle): Uses both an 
internal combustion engine and an electric 
motor; cannot be plugged in. 
●  PHEV (Plug -in Hybrid Electric Vehicle): Can 
be charged externally and also uses an interna l 
combustion engine. 
●  FCEV (Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle): Generates 
electricity onboard using hydrogen fuel cells. 
 
Critical Minerals for EV Batteries 
●  Lithium - Energy storage. 
●  Cobalt - Battery stability and energy density. 
●  Nickel - Improves battery capacity  and 
range. 
●  Graphite - Used in battery anodes. 
●  Rare Earth Elements (Neodymium, 
Dysprosium) - Used in permanent magnets of 
EV motors. 
 

 
Key Government Initiatives 
●  PM E -DRIVE Scheme (2024) - Promotes EV 
adoption and charging infrastructure. 
●  Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme 
for Advanced Chemistry Cells (ACC). 
●  PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto 
Components. 
●  National Electric Mobility Mission Plan 
(NEMMP) 2020. 
●  State EV Policies by states such as Tamil 
Nadu, Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Delhi. 
 
Advantages of EVs 
●  Zero tailpipe emissions. 
●  Lower operating and maintenance costs. 
●  Reduced dependence on imported crude oil. 
●  Lower noise pollution. 
●  Better energy efficiency than conventional 
vehicles. 
 
Challenges 
●  High initial purchase cost. 
●  Limited charging infrastructure. 
●  Battery disposal and recycling concerns. 
●  Dependence on imported critical minerals. 
●  Ethical and environmental concerns related 
to lithium and cobalt mining.

Statement 2:

sub-indices. The highest (worst) sub -index 
among the monitored pollutants determines the 
final AQI value .Hence, Statement 2 is 
incorrect. 
 
Statement 3: 
AQI is calculated only when data for a t least 
three pollutants is available, and either PM₂.₅ or

subject: Polity & Governance
question_text:
With reference  to the National Human 
Rights Commission (NHRC), consider the 
following statements: 
 
1. NHRC is a constitutional body. 
2. The Chairperson and members of NHRC are 
appointed by the President of India. 
3. NHRC can investigate complaints against 
armed forces in the sam e manner as ordinary 
public servants. 
 
Which of the statements given above is/are 
correct?
explanation:
Statement 1: NHRC is a constitutional body. 
The National Human Rights Commission is not a 
constitutional body  because it is not 
established by any provision of the Constitution 
of India.It is a statutory body established under 
the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 .A 
constitutional body derives its powers directly 
from the Constitution (e.g.,  Election 
Commission, Finance Commission, UPSC), 
whereas a statutory body is created through an 
Act of Parliament. Hence, Statement 1 is 
incorrect. 
 
Statement 2: The Chairperson and members 
of NHRC are appointed by the President of 
India 
The Chairperson and  Members of NHRC are 
appointed by the President of India  on the 
recommendations of a high -level committee 
consisting of: 
●  Prime Minister (Chairperson) 
●  Speaker of Lok Sabha 
●  Union Home Minister 
●  Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha 
●  Leaders of Opposition in Lok Sabha  and 
Rajya Sabha 
The appointment of a sitting Judge of the 
Supreme Court or a sitting Chief Justice of a 
High Court requires consultation with the Chief 
Justice of India.Hence, Statement 2 is correct. 
Statement 3: NHRC can investigate 
complaints against ar med forces in the same 
manner as ordinary public servants 
The Protection of Human Rights Act places 
restrictions on NHRC's jurisdiction over the 
armed forces.In cases involving armed forces: 
●  NHRC cannot conduct a direct investigation 
in the normal manner. 
●  It can seek a report from the Central 
Government. 
●  After examining the report, it may make 
recommendations to the Government. 
●  The Government must inform NHRC of the 
action taken within the prescribed period. 
Thus, NHRC's powers regarding armed forces 
are more limited than its powers over ordinary 
public servants. Hence, Statement 3 is 
incorrect.

Explanation 
1. Establishment of the North Eastern 
Council 
The North Eastern Council (NEC)  was 
constituted in 1971 under the North Eastern 
Council Act, 1971, enacted by Parliament. It is a 
statutory body created to promote coordinated 
development of the No rth Eastern Region.  
Hence, Statement 1 is correct. 
 
2. Role of the North Eastern Council 
The NEC functions as the nodal agency for the 
economic and social development  of the 
North Eastern Region. It acts as a regional 
planning body and supports infrastruct ure, 
connectivity, health, education, power, and 
 
other developmental projects. Hence, 
Statement 2 is correct. 
 
3. Composition of the North Eastern Region 
under NEC 
The North Eastern Region under NEC consists of 
eight states --Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, 
Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, 
Sikkim, and Tripura. Sikkim was included in the 
Council through the North Eastern Council 
(Amendment) Act, 2002 . Therefore, the region 
does not consist of only seven states.  Hence, 
Statement 3 is incorrect.

colonial period, after which it became one of the

subject: Polity & Governance
question_text:
With reference to Public Interest Litigation 
(PIL), consider the following statements: 
 
1. PIL can be filed by any public-spirited person 
for the protection of public interest, even if they 
are not personally affected by the issue. 
2. The concept of PIL in India was d eveloped 
through judicial activism of the Supreme Court 
during the 1980s. 
3. PIL can be filed against the Central 
Government, State Governments, and municipal 
authorities, but it cannot be filed against private 
parties alone. 
 
Which of the statements given ab ove are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
Statement 1: 
Public Interest Litigation (PIL) allows any 
public-spirited citizen or organization to 
approach the courts for the enforcem ent of 
rights of disadvantaged sections or for issues 
affecting the public at large, even if the 
petitioner is not personally aggrieved.  
 Hence, Statement 1 is correct. 
 
Statement 2: 
The concept of PIL evolved in India through 
judicial activism of the Supr eme Court in the 
late 1970s and 1980s. Justices such as P. N. 
Bhagwati and V. R. Krishna Iyer played a 
significant role in expanding access to justice 
through PIL. Hence, Statement 2 is correct. 
 
Statement 3: 
A PIL can be filed against the Central 
Government, State Governments, local bodies, 
statutory authorities, and public authorities for 
violation of constitutional or legal rights 
affecting the public. However, a PIL generally 
cannot be filed against a private individual or 
private entity alone unless th ere is a public duty 
or public law element involved.  Hence, 
Statement 3 is correct. 
 
Value Addition 
🔹 Constitutional Basis: Articles 32 and 226(not 
defined in Constitution) 
🔹 Objective: Access to justice for disadvantaged

Pariyojana, consider the following 
statements: 
 
1. Bharatmala Pariyojana is implemented by 
the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways 
(MoRTH) and seeks to improve the efficiency of

Quadrilateral and the North -South and East -

Corridors are identified primarily to improve 
freight movement across the country.

Which of the statements given above are

improving the efficiency of major National 
Corridors, including the Golden Quadrilateral 
and the North -South and East -West Corridors, 
by addressing congestion and infrastructure 
gaps. Hence, Statement 1 is correct. 
 
Statement 2: 
A major component of Bharatmala is the 
development of Economic Corridors to facilitate 
seamless freight movement, reduce logistics 
costs, and improve connectivity between

Statement 2 is correct.

subject: Polity & Governance
question_text:
With reference to the Public Accounts 
Committee (PAC), consider the following 
statements: 
 
1. The Public Accounts Committee is 
constituted every year by Parliament and its 
members are elected by the Lok Sabha and 
Rajya Sabha according to the principle of 
proportional representation by means of the 
single transferable vote.  
2. The Committee examines the reports of the 
Comptroller and Auditor  General (CAG) relating 
to government expenditure. 
3. A Union Minister can be appointed as a 
member of the Public Accounts Committee if 
nominated by the Speaker. 
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
1. The Public Accounts Committee is 
constituted every year by Parliament and its 
members are elected by the Lok Sabha and 
Rajya Sabha according to the principle of 
proportional representation by mea ns of the 
single transferable vote. 
 
The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) is 
constituted annually. It consists of 22 
members--15 elected by the Lok Sabha and 7 
elected by the Rajya Sabha according to the 
principle of proportional representation by 
means of th e single transferable vote . Hence, 
Statement 1 is correct. 
 
2. The Committee examines the reports of 
the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) 
relating to government expenditure. 
One of the primary functions of the PAC is to 
examine the audit reports submi tted by the 
Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India. 
It scrutinizes whether public money has been 
spent for the purpose approved by Parliament 
and in accordance with the rules.  Hence, 
Statement 2 is correct. 
 
3. A Union Minister can be appointed as a 
member of the Public Accounts Committee if 
nominated by the Speaker. 
Ministers are not eligible to be members of the 
Public Accounts Committee. If a member of the 
Committee is appointed as a Minister, he or she 
ceases to be a member of the PAC from the d ate 
of such appointment. Hence, Statement 3 is 
incorrect. 
 
Value Addition

Committee in India) 
🔹 Type: Financial Committee of Parliament 
🔹 Members: 22 (15 Lok Sabha + 7 Rajya Sabha) 
🔹 Term: One year 
🔹 Chairperson: Appointed by the Speaker of 
Lok Sabha, traditionally from the Opposition  
 🔹 Main Function:  Examines CAG reports and 
ensures proper utilization of public funds.

subject: Polity & Governance
question_text:
With reference to the National Bank for 
Agriculture and Rural Development 
(NABARD), consider the following 
statements: 
 
1. NABARD was established in 1982 through an 
Act of Parliament and functions as the apex 
development financial institution for agricultu re 
and rural development. 
2. NABARD provides refinance support to 
Cooperative Banks, Regional Rural Banks 
(RRBs), and Commercial Banks for lending to 
agriculture and rural sectors. 
3. NABARD manages the Rural Infrastructure 
Development Fund (RIDF), which finance s 
projects such as rural roads, bridges, and 
irrigation. 
4. NABARD acts as the implementing agency for 
the Interest Subvention Scheme for Cooperative 
Banks and RRBs, while RBI handles Scheduled 
Commercial Banks.  
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
Statement 1: NABARD was established in 
1982 through an Act of Parliament and 
functions as the apex development financial 
institution for agriculture and rural 
development. 
The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural 
Development (NABARD) was established on 12 
July 1982 under the NABARD Act, 1981. It was 
set up based on the recommendations of the 
Committee to Review Arrangements for 
Institutional Credit for Agriculture and Rural 
Development (CRAFICARD) headed by B. 
Sivaraman. NABARD serves as the apex 
institution for policy, planning, and operations 
 
relating to credit for agriculture and rural 
development in India. Hence, Statement 1 is 
correct. 
 
Statement 2: NABARD provides refinance 
support to Cooperative Banks, Regional 
Rural Banks (RRBs), and Commercial Banks 
for lending to agriculture and rural sectors. 
One of the core functions of NABARD is to 
provide refinance assistance to eligible fina ncial 
institutions such as State Cooperative Banks, 
District Central Cooperative Banks, Regional 
Rural Banks (RRBs), and Commercial Banks. 
This refinance enables these institutions to 
extend adequate credit for agriculture, allied 
activities, rural industr ies, and other 
developmental activities in rural areas.  Hence, 
Statement 2 is correct. 
 
Statement 3: NABARD manages the Rural 
Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF), 
which finances projects such as rural roads, 
bridges, and irrigation. 
The Rural Infrastruc ture Development Fund 
(RIDF) was established in 1995 -96 and is 
operated by NABARD. The fund supports State 
Governments and State -owned corporations in 
developing rural infrastructure such as roads, 
bridges, irrigation projects, flood protection 
works, drin king water facilities, health centres, 
and schools. RIDF plays a crucial role in 
reducing infrastructure gaps in rural India. 
Hence, Statement 3 is correct. 
 
Statement 4: NABARD has been designated 
as the implementing agency for the Interest 
Subvention Scheme (ISS) for short -term crop 
loans provided through cooperative banks 
and Regional Rural Banks. 
Under the Interest Subvention Scheme (ISS), 
farmers are provided short -term crop loans at 
concessional interest rates. NABARD acts as the 
implementing agency f or the scheme in respect 
of Cooperative Banks and Regional Rural Banks 
(RRBs), while the RBI handles scheduled 
commercial banks. Through this mechanism, 
NABARD facilitates timely flow of affordable 
agricultural credit to farmers.  Hence, 
Statement 4 is correct. 
 
Value Addition

🔹 Act: NABARD Act, 1981 
🔹 Headquarters: Mumbai 
🔹 Apex Institution for: Agriculture and Rural 
Development Finance 
🔹 RIDF Established: 1995-96 
🔹 Recommended by: CRAFICARD Committee 
(B. Sivaraman Committee) 
🔹 Major Programme: Self H elp Group -Bank 
Linkage Programme (SHG-BLP) 
🔹Shares supervisory functions over 
Cooperative Banks and RRBs with RBI.  
 🔹Owned by Government of India and RBI; 
administrative oversight through Department of 
Financial Services, Ministry of Finance.

subject: Economy
question_text:
With reference to the Monetary Policy 
Committee (MPC), consider the following 
statements: 
 
1. The Monetary Policy Committee was given a 
statutory basis through an am endment to the 
Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 in 2016. 
2. Three external members appointed by the 
Central Government from persons of ability, 
integrity and standing.  
3. In the event of a tie in voting, the Finance 
Minister of India exercises the casting vote. 
4. The MPC is required to meet at least four 
times in a year. 
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
Statement 1: The Monetary Policy C ommittee 
was given a statutory basis through an 
amendment to the Reserve Bank of India Act, 
1934 in 2016. 
The RBI Act, 1934 was amended in 2016 to 
provide a statutory basis for the Flexible 
Inflation Targeting (FIT) framework and the 
constitution of the Mo netary Policy Committee 
(MPC). Hence, Statement 1 is correct. 
 
Statement 2: The MPC consists of six 
members, of whom three are nominated by 
the Central Government. 
The MPC comprises six members: 
●  RBI Governor (Chairperson) 
●  RBI Deputy Governor in charge of M onetary 
Policy 
●  One RBI official nominated by the RBI Board 
●  Three external members appointed by the 
Central Government  Hence, Statement 2 is 
correct. 
 
Statement 3: In the event of a tie in voting, 
the Finance Minister of India exercises the 
casting vote. 
The MPC takes decisions by majority vote. In 
case of a tie, the RBI Governor, as Chairperson of 
the MPC, has the casting vote. The Finance 
Minister is not a member of the MPC.  Hence, 
Statement 3 is incorrect. 
 
Statement 4: The MPC is required to meet at 
least four times in a year. 
As per the RBI Act, the MPC must meet at least 
four times every year to determine the policy 
repo rate and formulate monetary policy.  
Hence, Statement 4 is correct. 
 
Value Addition 
🔹 Statutory Basis: RBI Act, 1934 (Amendment 
Act, 2016) 
🔹 Total Members: 6 
🔹 Government-Nominated Members: 3 
🔹 Chairperson: RBI Governor 
🔹 Inflation Target: 4% ± 2% (set by 
Government in consultation with RBI) 
🔹 Decision Making: Majority Vote 
🔹 Casting Vote: RBI Governor 
🔹 Minimum Meetings: 4 per year 
🔹 Objective: Maintain price stability while 
supporting economic growth

subject: Environment & Ecology
question_text:
With reference to Coral Re efs, consider 
the following statements: 
 
1. Coral reefs are formed by colonies of tiny 
marine animals known as coral polyps. 
2. Coral reefs are generally found in warm, 
shallow, and clear tropical waters. 
3. Coral reefs can thrive in regions with high 
sedimentation and low sunlight penetration. 
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
Statement 1: 
Coral reefs are formed by coral polyps, which 
are small m arine invertebrates belonging to the 
phylum Cnidaria. Over time, they secrete 
calcium carbonate skeletons that build reef 
structures. Hence, Statement 1 is correct. 
 
Statement 2: 
Most reef -building corals require warm 
temperatures (about 23°C -29°C), shallo w 
depths, and clear waters with adequate sunlight 
for the symbiotic algae (zooxanthellae) living 
within them. Hence, Statement 2 is correct. 
 
 
 
 
Statement 3: 
Coral reefs require clear water and abundant 
sunlight. High sedimentation and low light 
reduce phot osynthesis by zooxanthellae and 
hinder coral growth.  Hence, Statement 3 is 
incorrect. 
 
Value Addition

Reef 
🔹 Coral Reefs in India - Gulf of Mannar, Gulf of 
Kutch, Lakshadweep Islands, Andaman and 
Nicobar Islands 
🔹 Major Threats - Coral Bleaching, Ocean 
Acidification, Pollution, Overfishing 
🔹 Symbiotic Algae - Zooxanthellae provide food 
and colour to corals

question_text:
With reference to Lake Chad, consider the 
following statements: 
 
1. Lake Chad is shared by Chad, Cameroon, 
Nigeria, and Niger. 
2. The lake is situated in the Great Rift Valley of 
East Africa. 
 
Which of the statements given above is/are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
Statement 1: Lake Chad is shared by Chad, 
Cameroon, Nigeria, and Niger. 
Lake Chad is located in the Sahel region of west -
central Africa and is shared by four countries --
Chad, Cameroon, Nigeria, and Niger. Hence, 
Statement 1 is correct. 
 
Statement 2: The lake is situated in the Great 
Rift Valley of East Africa. 
Lake Chad is not located in the Great Rift Valley. 
It lies in the Lake Chad Basin in the Sahel region 
of west -central Africa. The Great Rift Valley is 
situated in eastern Africa and includes lakes 
such as Lake Tanganyika and Lake Malawi. 
Hence, Statement 2 is incorrect.

Nigeria, and Niger 
🔹 Type: Endorheic Lake (freshwater to slightly 
saline depending on season)

subject: Environment & Ecology
question_text:
Which one of the following is the first Plan 
Vivo-certified Reducing Emissions from 
Deforestation and Forest Degrada tion 
(REDD+) project in India?
option_b: ICFRE -ICIMOD Transboundary REDD+ Project in North-Eastern Himalayas
option_d: Sikkim Mamley Kamrang Community REDD+ Project
explanation:
Project 
Explanation 
Option (a): Uttarakhand REDD+ Project 
Uttarakhand has undertaken various forest 
conservation and carbon sequestration 
initiatives. However, it is not the first Plan 
Vivo-certified REDD+ project in India . Hence, 
Option (a) is incorrect. 
 
Option (b): ICFRE -ICIMOD Transboundary 
REDD+ Project in North-Eastern Himalayas 
This project was primarily focused on research, 
capacity building, and promotion of REDD+ 
strategies across the Himalayan region. It was 
not certified under the Plan Vivo Standard as 
India's first REDD+ project . Hence, Option 
(b) is incorrect. 
 
Option (c): Khasi Hills Community REDD+ 
Project 
The Khasi Hills Community REDD+ Project  in 
Meghalaya is India's first Plan Vivo -certified 
REDD+ project. It is a community -led initiative 
implemented by indigenous Khasi communities 
to reduce deforestation, conserve biodiversity, 
and improve livelihoods through sustainable 
forest management. The project received Plan 
Vivo certification in 2013. Hence, Option (c) 
is correct. 
 
Option (d): Sikkim Mamley Kamrang 
Community REDD+ Project 
Although Sikkim has undertaken several 
community-based conservation initiatives, the 
Mamley Kamrang project is not the first Plan 
Vivo-certified REDD+ project in India. Hence, 
Option (d) is incorrect. 
 
Value Addition 
🔹 REDD+ stands for Reducing Emissions from 
Deforestation and Forest Degradation , along 
with conservation of forest carbon stocks, 
sustainable management of forests, and 
enhancement of forest carbon stocks. 
🔹 Plan Vivo Standard  is an international 
certification framework that supports 
community-based climate change mitigation 
and ecosystem conservation projects. 
🔹 Khasi Hills Community REDD+ Project 
●  Location: East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya 
●  Area Covered: Approximately 27,000 
hectares 
●  Implemented by: Indigenou s Khasi 
communities 
●  Certification: Plan Vivo (2013) 
●  Objective: Forest conservation, carbon 
sequestration, biodiversity protection, and 
livelihood enhancement.

subject: Polity & Governance
question_text:
With reference to Bail in India, consider 
the following statements: 
 
1. Bail is a pre -trial release granted to an 
accused person while the case is pending before 
a court. 
2. The primary objective of bail is to ensure 
that the accused appears before the court 
during the trial. 
 
Which of the statements given above is/are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
1. Meaning of Bail as Pre -trial Release: Bail in 
India refers to the temporary release of an 
accused person from custody, subject to 
conditions imposed by the court, during the 
pendency of criminal proceedings. It is a key 
feature of criminal procedure under the Code of 
Criminal Procedure (CrPC), now replaced by the 
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 
2023. 
 
 
 
The essence of bail is to allow liberty to an 
accused before fin al adjudication, based on the 
principle that a person is presumed innocent 
until proven guilty. In this sense, bail operates 
as a mechanism of pre -trial liberty, ensuring 
that detention before conviction is not routine 
but exceptional. Hence, Statement 1 is correct. 
 
2. Objective of Ensuring Court Appearance: 
One of the fundamental objectives of bail under 
Bail in India is to ensure that the accused 
remains available for the trial process and does 
not evade justice. When courts grant bail, they 
impose condi tions such as bonds, sureties, and 
reporting requirements specifically to secure 
the presence of the accused during investigation 
and trial. 
 
This ensures that the administration of justice is 
not hampered and that the accused participates 
in the legal pro cess. Alongside protecting 
personal liberty, bail functions as a safeguard to 
ensure compliance with court proceedings. 
Hence, Statement 2 is correct. 
 
 🔹 Objective: Ensure the accused's appearance 
before the court while safeguarding personal 
liberty under Article 21. 
🔹 Types of Bail: Regular Bail, Anticipatory Bail, 
and Interim Bail. 
🔹 Principle: "Bail is the rule; jail is the 
exception".

subject: Environment & Ecology
question_text:
With reference to the Jai Prakash Narayan 
Bird Sanctuary, consider the following 
statements: 
 
1. It was designated as India's 100th Ramsar 
Site in 2026. 
2. Surha Taal, the core wetland of the 
sanctuary, is a natural perennial oxbow lake. 
3. The sanctuary serves as an important 
wintering ground for migratory birds along the 
Central Asian Flyway. 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
1. Designation as India's 100th Ramsar Site 
The Jai Prakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary, 
centred around Surha Taal in Uttar Pradesh, 
was designated as India's 100th Ramsar Site. 
Ramsar Sites are wetlands of internat ional 
importance recognised under the Ramsar 
Convention on Wetlands. This recognition 
highlights the ecological significance of the 
wetland and India's growing commitment to 
wetland conservation. Hence, Statement 1 is 
correct. 
 
2. Surha Taal as a Natural P erennial Oxbow 
Lake 
Surha Taal is a natural perennial oxbow lake 
formed due to changes in the course of the 
Ganga River. Oxbow lakes are crescent -shaped 
water bodies created when a river meander gets 
cut off from the main channel. The wetland 
retains water throughout the year and supports 
rich aquatic biodiversity, making it ecologically 
important. Hence, Statement 2 is correct. 
 
3. Importance Along the Central Asian 
Flyway 
The sanctuary is an important habitat for 
migratory birds arriving from regions such  as 
Central Asia and Siberia during winter. It forms 
part of the broader migratory route associated 
with the Central Asian Flyway. Several species 
of waterfowl and migratory birds use the 
wetland for feeding, breeding, and wintering 
purposes. Hence, Statement 3 is correct. 
 
🔹 Location: Ballia district, Uttar Pradesh. 
🔹 Wetland Type: Natural perennial oxbow lake. 
 
🔹 Ecological Importance: Habitat for migratory 
birds, fish diversity, and wetland biodiversity 
conservation. 
🔹 International Recognition: Declared a Ramsar 
Site under the Ramsar Convention on Wetlands. 
 
Value Addition 
The Central Asian Flyway (CAF)  is one of the 
world's major migratory bird flyways, covering 
migration routes of waterbirds and other 
migratory species between their breeding and 
wintering grounds. 
●  CAF is one of the nine major global 
flyways recognised for migratory birds. 
●   It links Arctic and Siberian breeding 
grounds with South Asian and Indian Ocean 
wintering grounds. 
●   India is a signatory to the Convention on 
Migratory Species (CMS)  and plays a key role 
in CAF conservation. 
 
🔹 Countries Covered 
The flyway covers 30 countries , including 
India, Russia, Kazakhstan, Mongolia, China, 
Afghanistan, Pakistan, Nepal, Bhutan, 
Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and the Maldives. 
🔹 Importance for India 
India lies at the h eart of the Central Asian 
Flyway and provides crucial wintering, staging, 
and breeding habitats for numerous migratory 
bird species. 
🔹 Migratory Birds Using CAF 
●  Siberian Crane, Bar -headed Goose, Greater 
Flamingo, Black-tailed Godwit, Northern Pintail 
🔹 Key Indian Wetlands on CAF 
●  Keoladeo National Park 
●  Chilika Lake 
●  Sambhar Lake 
●  Harike Wetland 
●  Jai Prakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary

subject: Economy
question_text:
Consider the following pairs: 
Tool Description 
1.Liquidity 
Adjustment 
Facility (LAF) 
Enables banks to borrow from 
and lend to the RBI through 
Repo and Reverse Repo 
operations 
2.Statutory 
Liquidity Ratio 
(SLR) 
The percentage of deposits that 
banks must maintain with the 
RBI in cash 
3.Marginal 
Standing Facility  
(MSF) 
MSF allows Scheduled 
Commercial Banks to borrow 
overnight funds from the RBI 
during emergency liquidity 
shortages.  
 
How many of the above pairs are correctly 
matched?
explanation:
Explanation 
Pair 1: Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) - 
Enables banks to borrow from and lend to 
RBI through Repo and Reverse Repo 
operations 
The Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) is a 
monetary policy tool used by RBI to manage 
short-term liquidity in the bank ing system. It 
operates through Repo and Reverse Repo 
transactions. Hence, Pair 1 is correctly 
matched. 
 
Pair 2: Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) - 
Percentage of deposits that banks must 
maintain with the RBI in cash 
This is incorrect. Under SLR, banks main tain a 
specified percentage of their Net Demand and 
Time Liabilities (NDTL) in the form of cash, 
gold, or approved securities. These assets are 
 
maintained by the banks themselves and need 
not be deposited with the RBI.  Hence, Pair 2 is 
incorrectly matched. 
 
Pair 3: Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) - A 
facility through which Scheduled 
Commercial Banks can borrow overnight 
funds from RBI after exhausting LAF options 
MSF allows Scheduled Commercial Banks to 
borrow overnight funds from RBI during 
emergencies when liquidity available under LAF 
is insufficient . Hence, Pair 3 is correctly 
matched. 
 
Value Addition 
🔹 Liquidity Adjustment Facility → Repo Rate & 
Reverse Repo Rate 
🔹 Statutory Liquid Ratio → Maintained by 
banks in cash, gold, and approved securities 
🔹 Cash Reserve Ratio → Maintained with RBI in 
cash; no interest paid 
🔹 Marginal Standing Facility → Em ergency 
overnight borrowing window for banks 
🔹 Open Market Operations → RBI buys/sells 
government securities to manage liquidity 
🔹 Market Stabilisation Scheme → Used to 
absorb excess liquidity through Market      
Stabilisation Bonds (MSBs)

subject: Geography
question_text:
Which of the following water bodies is 
connected to the Black Sea through the Strait 
of Kerch?
explanation:
Explanation 
Option (a): Sea of Azov 
The Sea of Azov is located north of the Black Sea 
and is directly connected to it through the Strait 
of Kerch. The strait serves as the only natural 
maritime link between the two water bodies.  
Hence, Option (a) is correct. 
 
 
Option (b): Caspian Sea 
The Caspian Sea is the world's largest inland 
water body and is landlocked. It has no natural 
connection with the Black Sea and is separated 
from it by the Caucasus region. Hence, Option 
(b) is incorrect. 
 
 
Option (c): Adriatic Sea 
The Adriatic Sea is a part of the Mediterranean 
Sea located between the Italian Peninsula and 
the Balkan Peninsula. It is not connected to the 
Black Sea through the Strait of Kerch . Hence, 
Option (c) is incorrect. 

 
 
 
Option (d): Aegean Sea 
The Aegean Sea is conne cted to the Black Sea 
indirectly through the Turkish Straits system 
(Bosporus-Sea of Marmara -Dardanelles), not 
through the Strait of Kerch.  Hence, Option (d) 
is incorrect. 
 
Value Addition 
 🔹 Strait of Kerch → Connects the Sea of Azov 
and the Black Sea 
🔹 Sea of Azov → Shallowest sea in the world 
🔹 Caspian Sea → Largest inland water body 
(landlocked) 
🔹 Bosporus Strait → Connects Black Sea and Sea 
of Marmara 
🔹 Dardanelles Strait → Connects the Sea of 
Marmara and the Aegean Sea 
🔹 Aegean Sea → Part of the  Mediterranean Sea 
system 
 🔹 Major Rivers draining into the Sea of Azov → 
Don and Kuban Rivers

subject: Polity & Governance
question_text:
With reference to the National 
Commission for Women (NCW), co nsider the 
following statements: 
 
1. The National Commission for Women is a 
statutory body established under the National 
Commission for Women Act, 1990. 
2. The Chairperson, Members, and Member -
Secretary of the NCW are nominated by the 
Central Government. 
3. The recommendations made by the NCW are 
legally binding on the Central and State 
Governments. 
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
1. NCW as a S tatutory Body: The National 
Commission for Women (NCW) is a statutory 
body established under the National 
Commission for Women Act, 1990. It was set up 
in 1992 to review constitutional and legal 
safeguards for women, recommend remedial 
legislative measures , and facilitate grievance 
redressal. 
 As a statutory body, it derives its authority 
from an Act of Parliament rather than directly 
from the Constitution.  Hence, Statement 1 is 
correct. 
 
2. Appointment by the Central Government: 
Under the provisions of the  NCW Act, the 
Chairperson, five Members, and the Member -
Secretary are nominated by the Central 
Government. The Chairperson is generally a 

 
person committed to the cause of women, while 
Members are selected from fields such as law, 
administration, women's we lfare, labour 
movements, and social work. Hence, Statement 
2 is correct. 
 
3. Nature of NCW Recommendations: The 
recommendations made by the NCW are 
advisory in nature and are not legally binding 
on the Central or State Governments.  
 The Commission can inve stigate complaints, 
recommend policy changes, and suggest legal 
reforms, but it does not possess judicial powers 
to enforce its recommendations.  Hence, 
Statement 3 is incorrect. 
 
Value Addition 
🔹 Established: 1992 
🔹 Act: National Commission for Women Act , 
1990 
🔹 Type: Statutory Body 
🔹 Composition: Chairperson + 5 Members + 
Member-Secretary 
🔹 Tenure: 3 Years 
🔹 Nominated By: Central Government 
🔹 Powers: Powers of a Civil Court while 
investigating matters 
🔹 Functions: Review safeguards for women, 
investigate complaints, recommend legal

subject: Environment & Ecology
question_text:
With reference to E85 fuel and Flex -Fuel 
Vehicles (FFVs) in India, consider the 
following statements: 
 
1. E85 is a fuel blend consisting of 80 -85% 
ethanol and the remaining portion of petrol. 
2. Flex-Fuel Vehicles can operate only on E20 
fuel blends. 
3. Higher ethanol blends, such as E85, help 
reduce greenhouse gas emissions compared to 
conventional petrol vehicles. 
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
1. Composition of E85 Fuel 
E85 is  a high -ethanol blended fuel comprising 
about 80-85% ethanol and 14 -19% petrol. It is 
specifically designed for use in Flex -Fuel 
Vehicles (FFVs). The initiative is aimed at 
promoting cleaner fuels and reducing 
dependence on imported crude oil.  Hence, 
Statement 1 is correct. 
 
2. Flex-Fuel Vehicles and Fuel Compatibility 
Flex-Fuel Vehicles (FFVs) are specially designed 
vehicles capable of operating on a wide range of 
ethanol blends, from E20 to E100. They are not 
restricted only to E20 fuel. This flexibility allows 
consumers to use different ethanol -petrol 
blends depending on availability.  Hence, 
Statement 2 is incorrect. 
 
3. Environmental Benefits of E85 
Higher ethanol blends such as E85 significantly 
reduce lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions 
compared to conv entional petrol vehicles. E85 
also promotes cleaner combustion with near -
zero particulate matter emissions, thereby 
contributing to improved urban air quality. 
Hence, Statement 3 is correct. 
 
🔹 E85 Fuel: Blend containing 80-85% ethanol. 
🔹 FFVs: Vehicles capable of operating on 
multiple ethanol blends from E20 to E100. 
🔹 Benefits: Reduced crude oil imports, lower 
emissions, support to farmers, and foreign 
exchange savings. 
🔹 Ethanol Source: Primarily produced from 
agricultural feedstock such as sugarcane and 
grains.

question_text:
With reference to the Europe an Union 
(EU), consider the following statements: 
 
1. The European Union is a political and 
economic union of European countries. 
2. All member states of the European Union use 
the Euro as their official currency. 
3. The European Commission acts as the 
executive arm of the European Union. 
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
1. Nature of the European Union 
The European Union (EU) is a unique politica l 
and economic union comprising European 
countries that cooperate in areas such as trade, 
security, lawmaking, climate policy, and free 
movement of people and goods.  
 It evolved from post -World War II economic 
cooperation initiatives aimed at promoting 
 
peace and integration in Europe.  Hence, 
Statement 1 is correct. 
 
2. Use of the Euro by Member States 
Not all EU member states use the Euro as their 
official currency. While many countries are part 
of the Eurozone, some members such as Poland, 
Hungary, Sweden, and Denmark continue to use 
their national currencies. Therefore, Euro 
adoption is not mandatory for all EU members 
immediately upon joining. Hence, Statement 2 
is incorrect. 
 
3. European Commission as the Executive 
Arm 
The European Commission functions a s the 
executive body of the EU. It proposes legislation, 
implements EU decisions, upholds treaties, and 
manages the day -to-day functioning of the 
Union. It plays a central role in policymaking 
and governance within the EU institutional 
framework. Hence, Statement 3 is correct. 
 
🔹 Headquarters: Brussels, Belgium 
🔹 Current Members: 27 countries. 
🔹 Key Institutions: European Commission, 
European Parliament, European Council, Court 
of Justice of the EU, and European Central Bank. 
🔹 Eurozone: Group of EU countries that use the 
Euro currency.

subject: Economy
question_text:
With reference to the Reserve Bank of 
India (RBI), consider the following 
statements: 
 
1. The Reserve Bank of India was established 
under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. 
2. The RBI is responsible for issuing and 
managing the currency of India except the one -
rupee note and coins. 
3. The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is 
headed by the Union Finance Minister. 
 
Which of the statements given abo ve are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
1. Establishment of RBI 
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was 
established under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 
1934, and began functionin g on 1 April 1935. 
Initially headquartered in Kolkata, it was later 
permanently shifted to Mumbai in 1937. The 
RBI was nationalised in 1949 after 
Independence. It serves as India's central bank 
and is responsible for regulating the country's 
monetary and f inancial system.  Hence, 
Statement 1 is correct. 
 
2. Currency Issuance Function 
The RBI has the sole authority to issue and 
manage currency notes in India except the one -
rupee note and coins, which are issued by the 
Government of India through the Ministry of 
Finance. Although coins and one -rupee notes 
are issued by the government, they are 
circulated through the RBI. The RBI also 
manages currency circulation, replacement of 
damaged notes, and maintenance of adequate 
liquidity in the economy. Hence, Statement 2 is 
correct. 
 
3. Head of the Monetary Policy Committee 
The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is 
chaired by the Governor of the RBI and not by 
the Union Finance Minister. The MPC was 
constituted under the RBI Act, 1934, through 
amendments made in 2016 to i nstitutionalise 
inflation targeting in India. It consists of six 
members -- three from the RBI and three 
external members appointed by the 
Government of India. 
 
 
The committee decides the policy repo rate to 
maintain price stability while supporting 
economic growth. Hence, Statement 3 is 
incorrect. 
 
🔹 RBI Motto: "Yogakshemam Vahamyaham" 
(taken from the Bhagavad Gita). 
🔹 Headquarters: Mumbai, Maharashtra. 
🔹 Current Monetary Framework: Flexible 
Inflation Targeting with a target of 4% CPI 
inflation ± 2%. 
🔹 Major Functions: Banker to the Government, 
banker's bank, regulator of banks, manager of 
foreign exchange reserves, and issuer of 
currency. 
🔹 Important Monetary Tools: Repo Rate, 
Reverse Repo Rate, Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), 
and Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR).

areas.

Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
1. WFP as a UN Agency Fighting Hunger 
The Wo rld Food Programme (WFP) is the food 
assistance branch of the United Nations and is 
the world's largest humanitarian organisation 
addressing hunger and food insecurity. It 
provides emergency food assistance during 
conflicts, natural disasters, and humanita rian 
crises while also supporting nutrition, school 
feeding, and livelihood programmes.  Hence, 
Statement 1 is correct. 
 
2. Nobel Peace Prize 2020 
The WFP received the Nobel Peace Prize in 
2020 for its efforts to combat hunger, improve 
conditions for peace in conflict zones, and 
prevent the use of hunger as a weapon of war.  
The award highlighted the strong connection 
between food security and global peace and 
stability. Hence, Statement 2 is correct. 
 
3. Headquarters of WFP 
The headquarters of the World Food  
Programme is located in Rome, Italy, and not in 
Geneva, Switzerland. Rome also hosts other 
major UN food -related agencies such as the 
Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and 
the International Fund for Agricultural 
Development (IFAD). Hence, Statement 3 is 
incorrect.

🔹 Core Objective:  Achieving Zero Hunger and 
ensuring food security during emergencies and 
conflicts. 
🔹 Major Activities:  Emergency food aid, 
nutrition support, sc hool meals, logistics 
assistance, and humanitarian relief operations.
