question_text:
With reference to the Ordinance -making 
power of the President of India, consider the 
following statements: 
 
1. The President can promulgate an Ordinance 
when either House of Parliament is not in 
session.  
2. An Ordinance has the same force and effect 
as an Act of Parliament. 
 
3. An Ordinance can be used to amend the 
Constitution of India. 
 
Which of the statem ents given above are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
Statement 1: 
Under Article 123, the President may 
promulgate an Ordinance when either House of 
Parliament is not in session and  circumstances 
exist which require immediate action.  An 
Ordinance can be issued when at least one 
House is not in session, since Parliament cannot 
enact a law unless both Houses are available to 
pass it. Hence, Statement 1 is correct. 
 
Statement 2: 
An Ordi nance has the same force and effect as 
an Act of Parliament, though it is temporary in 
nature. Hence, Statement 2 is correct. 
 
Statement 3: 
An Ordinance cannot amend the Constitution. 
Constitutional amendments can be made only 
through the procedure prescri bed under Article 
368. Hence, Statement 3 is incorrect. 
 
Value Addition 
🔹 Constitutional Provision: Article 123 
🔹 Issued By: President of India 
🔹 Nature: Temporary law during Parliament's 
recess 
🔹 Validity: Up to 6 weeks from reassembly of 
Parliament (unless approved earlier or 
disapproved) 
🔹 Can Amend: Ordinary laws, including tax laws 
🔹 Cannot Amend: Constitution of India 
🔹 Judicial Review: Permissible

●  UNESCO World Heritage Site and Tiger

designations together.hence (a) is incorrect 
(b)Manas National Park 
Manas National Park is located in Assam along 
the India -Bhutan border and derives its name 
from the Manas River, a major tributary of the 
Brahmaputra. It is renowned for possessing 
multiple international and national 
conservation designations simultaneously: 
●  UNESCO Natural World Heritage Site 
●  Tiger Reserve 
●  Elephant Reserve 
●  Biosphere Reserve 
●  Important Bird Area (IBA) 
 
The park is also famous for rare species such as 
the Pygmy Hog, Hispid Hare, Golden Langur, and 
Wild Water Buffalo.hence (b) is correct

Brahmaputra)

included in 1973

landscape with Royal Manas National Park  in 
Bhutan  
(c) Nameri National Park 
●  Located in Assam along the foothills of the 
Eastern Himalayas. 
●  Famous for White-winged Wood Duck  and 
river rafting on the Jia Bhoroli River. 
●  Tiger Reserve landscape but not a UNESCO 
World Heritage Site.hence (c) is incorrect

rhinoceros.

tags.hence (d) is incorrect

76. Compensatory Afforestation Fund 
Management & Planning 
Authority(CAMPA) 
Q. With reference to the Compensatory 
Afforestation Fund Management and 
Planning Authority (CAMPA), consider the 
following statements: 
 
1. The National Compensatory Afforestation 
Fund is maint ained under the Public Account of 
India. 
2. CAMPA was established by the Supreme 
Court to monitor and evaluate compensatory 
afforestation activities. 
3. Under the Compensatory Afforestation Fund 
Act, 2016, the entire fund collected is retained 
by the Central Government. 
 
How many of the statements given above are 
correct? 
 
(a) Only one 
(b) Only two 
(c) All three 
(d) None 
 
Answer: (b) Only two 
 
Explanation 
Statement 1: 
The Compensatory Afforestation Fund (CAF) 
Act, 2016 created: 
●  National Compensatory Afforestation Fund 
(NCAF) under the Public Account of India. 
●  State Compensatory Afforestation Funds 
(SCAF) under the Public Account of the 
respective States. 
The money collected from user agencies for 
diversion of forest land is deposited in these 
funds and utilized for  afforestation and forest 
conservation activities. Hence, statement 1 is 
correct. 
Statement 2: 
The Supreme Court established CAMPA in 2002 
as an ad hoc body to: 
●  Monitor compensatory afforestation 
activities. 
●  Provide technical assistance. 
●  Evaluate afforestation projects. 
●  Administer the funds collected for 
compensatory afforestation. 
CAMPA was created because large amounts of 
money collected for forest diversion were lying 
unutilized.Hence, statement 2 is correct. 
Statement 3:  
The CAF Act, 2016 does not allow  the Central 
Government to retain the entire fund. 
Instead: 
●  90% of the funds are transferred to the 
respective State Compensatory Afforestation 
Funds. 
●  10% remains in the National Compensatory 
Afforestation Fund. Hence, statement 3 is 
incorrect. 
Value Addition  
●   Established: CAMPA (2002) by Supreme 
Court 
●   CAF Act: 2016, Rules Notified: 2018 
●   Fund Distribution: States - 90% ,Centre - 
10% 
●  CAF funds are non-lapsable.  
●   Accounts: National CAF → Public Account of 
India, State CAF → Public Account of respective 
States 
●   Compensatory Afforestation:When forest 
land is diverted for non -forest purposes 
(mining, industries, roads, dams etc.), the user 
agency must:  Provide equivalent non -forest 
land for afforestation, or     Provide twice the 
area of degraded forest land if non-forest land is 
unavailable. 
●   Funds can be used for:Afforestation and 
reforestation,Wildlife protection and 
management, Catchment area treatment,Forest 
management,Human-wildlife conflict 
mitigation,Relocation of villages from protected 
areas

78. Chief Justice of India (CJI) 
8.With reference t o the Chief Justice of India 
(CJI), consider the following statements: 
 
1. The Chief Justice of India is appointed by the 
President of India under Article 124(2). 
2. The Chief Justice of India administers the 
oath of office to the President of India. 
3. The Chief J ustice of India can be removed 
from office by the President on the 
recommendation of the Prime Minister. 
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct? 
 
(a) 1 and 2 only 
(b) 2 and 3 only 
 (c) 1 and 3 only 
(d) 1, 2 and 3 
 
Answer: (a) 1 and 2 only 
Explanation 
Statement 1: 
The Chief Justice of India is appointed by the 
President of India under Article 124(2). 
●  Article 124(2)  of the Constitution provides 
that every Judge of the Supreme Court, including 
the Chief Justice of India, shall be appointed by 
the President. 
●  By convention, the senior-most judge of the 
Supreme Court is appointed as the Chief Justice 
of India. 
●  Retirement Age: 65 years  
●  The appointment process is now guided by 
the Collegium System, evolved through judicial 
pronouncements.Hence, Statement 1 is 
correct. 
Statement 2:  
The Chief Justice of India administers the 
oath of office to the President of India. 
●  According to Article 60  of the Constitution, 
the President takes the oath before the Chief 
Justice of India. 
●  In the absence of the CJI, the oat h is 
administered by the senior-most available Judge 
of the Supreme Court. 
●  This highlights the constitutional importance 
and ceremonial role of the office of the 
CJI.Hence, Statement 2 is correct. 
Statement 3: 
The Chief Justice of India can be removed 
from office by the President on the 
recommendation of the Prime Minister. 
●  The CJI cannot be removed merely on the 
recommendation of the Prime Minister. 
●  Like all Supreme Court judges, the CJI can be 
removed only under Article 124(4)  on the 
grounds of: 
○ Proved misbehaviour, or 
○ Incapacity. 
Removal Procedure 
1. A motion is introduced in either House of 
Parliament. 
2. The motion must be passed by a special 
majority in both Houses: 
○ Majority of the total membership of the 
House, and 
○ Two-thirds of members present and voting. 
3. After Parliament passes the motion, the 
President issues the removal order. 
This rigorous procedure ensures the 
independence of the judiciary  and protects 
judges from arbitrary removal. Hence 
Statement 3 is incorrect.

question_text:
Consider the following statements:   
 
I. India has joined the Minerals Security 
Partnership as a member.   
II. India is a resource -rich country in all the 30 
critical minerals that it has identified.   
III. The Parliament in 2023 has amended the 
Mines and Minerals (Development and 
Regulation) Act, 1957 empowering the Central 
Government to exclusively auction mining lease 
and composite license for cer tain critical 
minerals.    
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
Statement I: Correct 
India has joined the Minerals Secu rity 
Partnership (MSP) as a member. 
●  The Minerals Security Partnership (MSP)  
is a US-led initiative launched in 2022. 
 
●  It aims to strengthen secure, sustainable and 
resilient supply chains for critical minerals such 
as lithium, cobalt, nickel, graphite and rare earth 
elements. 
●  India became a member of the MSP in 
2023.hence, Statement I is correct. 
Statement II:  
India is a resource -rich country in all the 30 
critical minerals that it has identified. 
●  India has identified 30 critical minerals  
essential for econ omic development, energy 
transition and strategic sectors. 
●  However, India is not resource-rich in all of 
them. 
●  Several critical minerals such as lithium, 
cobalt, nickel and certain rare earth 
elements are available only in limited 
quantities domestically, leading to import 
dependence.Hence, Statement II is incorrect. 
Statement III: 
The Parliament in 2023 amended the MMDR 
Act, 1957 empowering the Central 
Government to auction certain critical 
minerals. 
●  The Mines and Minerals (Development 
and Regulation) Amen dment Act, 2023  
introduced major reforms in the mining sector. 
●  It empowered the Central Government  to 
exclusively auction mining leases and composite 
licences for specified critical and strategic 
minerals. 
●  The amendment aimed to encourage 
exploration and d omestic production of critical 
minerals needed for clean energy technologies 
and advanced manufacturing.Hence, Statement 
III is correct.

western shore of the Red Sea. It also includes

Strait, which forms the southern gateway of the

It lies south of Djibouti and has coastlines along 
the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean.

the Red Sea and has an important maritime 
outlet through Port Sudan.

question_text:
With reference to the Munda Rebellion 
(Ulgulan), consider the following statements: 
 
1. Birsa Munda led the rebellion in the 
Chotanagpur region against British rule and 
exploitative landlords. 
2. The rebellion was primarily directed against 
the Permanent Settlement introduced in Bengal. 
3. One of the important outcomes of the 
movement was the enactment of the 
Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908. 
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
1. The Munda Rebellion, also known as Ulgulan 
(Great Tumult), was led by Birsa Munda 
between 1899 and 1900 in the Chotanagpur 
Plateau region. It was directed against British 
colonial rule, landlords, outsiders(dikus), 
moneylenders, and contractors who had 
dispossessed tribals of their traditional land 
rights. Hence, Statement 1 is correct. 
 
2. The rebellion was not primarily against the 
Permanent Settlement. The main grievance was 
the destruction of the traditional Khunt katti 
system of communal land ownership and the 
intrusion of zamindars, thikadars, and 
moneylenders into tribal lands . Hence, 
Statement 2 is incorrect. 
 
3. One of the major long -term outcomes of the 
rebellion was the enactment of the Chotanagpur 
Tenancy Act, 1908, which restricted the transfer 
of tribal land to non -tribals and provided legal 
protection to tribal land rights . Hence, 
Statement 3 is correct.

Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY), consider the

How many of the statements given above are

question_text:
With reference to Gallantry Aw ards in 
India, consider the following statements: 
 
1. Kirti Chakra is the second -highest peacetime 
gallantry award and is awarded for conspicuous 
courage, valour or self -sacrifice away from the 
battlefield.  
2. Vir Chakra is awarded for acts of gallantry in 
the presence of the enemy. 
3. Ashoka Chakra is the highest wartime 
gallantry award in India. 
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
1. Kirti Chakra  is the second -highest peacetime 
gallantry award and is awarded for 
distinguished acts of bravery not involving 
direct engagement with the enemy. Kirti Chakra 
is India's second -highest peacetime gallantry 
award, ranking below Ashoka Chakra and above 
 
Shaurya Chakra. It is awarded for conspicuous 
courage, valour or self -sacrifice away from the 
battlefield. Hence, Statement 1 is correct. 
 
2. Vir Chakra is awarded for acts of gallantry in 
the presence of the enemy.Vir Chakra is the 
third-highest wartime gallant ry award and is 
conferred for acts of gallantry performed in the 
presence of the enemy. Hence, Statement 2 is 
correct. 
 
3. Ashoka Chakra is the highest wartime 
gallantry award in India. Ashoka Chakra is the 
highest peacetime gallantry award, not a 
wartime award. The highest wartime gallantry 
award is the Param Vir Chakra.  Hence, 
Statement 3 is incorrect.

question_text:
The term 'Orobanche aegyptiaca' (locally 
called Margoja), recently seen in the news, is 
best known as:
option_a: A root -parasitic flowering weed affecting mustard and other crops
option_b: A fungal pathogen causing rust disease in oilseed crops
option_c: A nitrogen -fixing bacterium used to improve soil fertility
option_d: An invasive insect pest that damages stored food grains
explanation:
affecting mustard and other crops 
Explanation 
1. Orobanche aegyptiaca (Margoja) is a root -
parasitic flowering weed that attaches itself to 
the roots of crops such as mustard and extracts 
water, carbon and nutrients from the host plant. 
It can cause severe yield losses and is a major 
challenge in mustard cultivation, particularly in 
north-western India. Hence, Option (a) is 
correct. 
2. Orobanche is not a fungus. It is a flowering 
parasitic plant. Hence, Option (b) is incorrect. 
3. Nitrogen-fixing bacteria, such as Rhizobium, 
improve soil fertility, whereas Orobanche is a 
harmful parasitic weed. Hence, Option (c) is 
incorrect. 
4. Orobanche is neither an insect nor a storage 
pest. Hence, Option (d) is incorrect. 
Value Addition 
●  Scientific Name: Orobanche aegyptiaca (also 
referred to as Phelipanche aegyptiaca) 
●   Local Name: Margoja 
●  Nature: Root-parasitic flowering weed 
●  Origin: Mediterranean-West Asian region 
●  Major Host Crop: Mustard 
●  Distribution in India:  Rajasthan, Haryana 
and other mustard-growing regions 
●  Seed Viability: Can remain vi able in soil for 
up to 20 years 
●  Spread: Wind, irrigation water, 
contaminated soil and farm implements 
●   Impact: Causes a severe reduction in crop 
yield by extracting nutrients and water from 
host plants. 
●   Control: IMI-resistant mustard hybrids 
developed thr ough mutation breeding.

90. Quantum entanglement and 
superposition 
Q. With reference to Quantum Mechanics, 
consider the following statements: 
 
1. Superposition allows a quantum particle to 
exist in multipl e states simultaneously until it is 
measured. 
2. Quantum entanglement refers to a 
phenomenon in which the state of one particle 
is correlated with that of another, regardless of 
the distance separating them. 
 
Which of the statements given above is/are 
correct? 
 
(a) 1 only 
(b) 2 only 
(c) Both 1 and 2 
(d) Neither 1 nor 2 
 
Answer: (c) Both 1 and 2 
Explanation: 
1. Superposition allows a quantum particle to 
exist in multiple states simultaneously until it is 
measured. Superposition is a fundamental 
principle of qua ntum mechanics according to 
which a quantum system can exist in several 
possible states at the same time. Upon 
measurement, the system collapses into one 
definite state. For example, a quantum bit 
(qubit) can represent both 0 and 1 
simultaneously until it is observed. Hence, 
Statement 1 is correct. 
2. Quantum entanglement refers to a 
phenomenon in which the state of one particle 
is correlated with that of another, regardless of 
the distance separating them. Quantum 
 
entanglement occurs when two or more 
particles become linked in such a way that the 
measurement outcomes remain correlated 
regardless of distance, even if they are 
separated by large distances. This phenomenon 
is the basis of emerging technologies such as 
quantum communication and quantum 
cryptography. Hence, Statement 2 is correct. 
Value Addition 
🔹 Superposition: A quantum particle can exist 
in multiple possible states simultaneously until 
measured. 
🔹 Quantum Entanglement:  Two or more 
particles remain correlated such that measuring 
one reveals a correlated state of the other.  
🔹 Qubit: Basic unit of quantum computing that 
can exist as 0, 1, or a superposition of both. 
🔹 Quantum Computing:  Uses principles of 
superposition and entanglement to perform 
complex computations faster than classical 
computers for certain problems. 
🔹 Applications: Quantum computing, quantum 
communication, quantum cryptography, 
quantum sensing, and secure data transmission. 
🔹 Nobel Prize 2022:  Awarded to Alain Aspect, 
John F. Clauser, and Anton Zeilinger for 
experiments with entangled photons

subject: Polity & Governance
question_text:
With reference to the composition and 
election of the Rajya Sabha, consider the 
following statements: 
 
1. Members of the Rajya Sabha are elected by 
the elected members of Stat e Legislative 
Assemblies through the system of Proportional 
Representation by Single Transferable Vote. 
2. The Governor of a State has the authority to 
nominate members to the Rajya Sabha from that 
State. 
3. Rajya Sabha is a permanent House and is 
never dissolved as a whole.
explanation:
1. Election Method of Rajya Sabha Members: 
●  Constitutional Provision:  Article 80(4) of 
the Constitution states that the representatives 
of each State in the Rajya Sabha shall be elected 
by the elected me mbers of the Legislative 
Assembly of that State in accordance with the 
system of Proportional Representation by 
means of the Single Transferable Vote (STV). 
 
●  The open ballot system for Rajya Sabha 
elections was introduced by the 
Representation of the Peopl e (Amendment) 
Act, 2003  -- a Parliamentary statute , not a 
Constitutional Amendment Act. Voting is 
conducted by open ballot  -- an MLA must 
show their ballot to their party's authorised 
agent, preventing secret cross-voting. 
 
●
value_addition:
Nominated MLAs cannot vote in Rajya 
Sabha elections -- only elected members of the 
Legislative Assembly can. Hence, Statement 1 
is correct.  
2. Nomination Power -- President, Not 
Governor 
●  The Governor has NO role  in nominating 
members to the Rajya Sabha. 
●  Under Article 80(1)(a) , it is t he President 
of India  who nominates 12 members  to the 
Rajya Sabha from among persons having special 
knowledge or practical experience in: 
○ Literature, Science, Art, Social Service 
●  The Governor's nomination power is limited 
to the State Legislative Council ( Vidhan 
Parishad) under Article 171(5) , not to the 
Rajya Sabha. Hence, Statement 2 is incorrect.  
3. Permanent Character of Rajya Sabha 
●  Constitutional Provision:  Under Article 
83(1), the Rajya Sabha is a permanent body  
and cannot be dissolved. 
●  One-third of its members retire every two 
years, ensuring continuity of the House. 
●  Members are elected for a six-year term  
each. 
 
●  This is in contrast to the Lok Sabha , which 
has a normal term of five years  and can be 
dissolved earlier by the President on the advice 
of t he Council of Ministers under Article 
85(2)(b). 
●  The permanent character  of the Rajya 
Sabha ensures that legislative business is never 
completely disrupted. Hence, Statement 3 is 
correct.

question_text:
With reference to the Viksit Bharat -
Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission 
(Gramin) [VB -G RAM G] Act, 2025, consider 
the following statements: 
 
1. The Act guarantees 125 days of wage 
employment per rural household in a financial 
year. 
2. The Act provides for a state -notified no-work 
period during peak sowing and harvesting 
seasons. 
3. The financial responsibility for 
implementation of the scheme rests entirely 
with the Union Government.  
4. Social audits under the Act are mandated at 
least once every six months. 
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
1. Enhanced Employment Guarantee: The Viksit 
Bharat-G RAM G Act,  2025 guarantees 125 days 
of wage employment per rural household per 
financial year, increasing the entitlement from 
the 100 days provided under MGNREGA. Hence, 
Statement 1 is correct. 
 
2. Agricultural Labour Protection: The Act 
provides for an aggregated 60-day no -work 
period, to be notified by States during peak 
sowing and harvesting seasons. This provision 
seeks to ensure the availability of agricultural 
labour during critical farming operations. 
Workers continue to retain their entitlement to 
125 days o f guaranteed employment, which 
must be provided during the remaining part of 
the year. Hence, Statement 2 is correct. 
 
3. Funding Architecture: The Act shifts the rural 
employment programme from a largely Centre -
funded framework to a Centrally Sponsored 
Scheme with explicit Centre -State cost -sharing 
norms. Instead, it adopts a cost -sharing 
framework: 
●  60:40 between Centre and States (general 
states) 
●  90:10 for North -Eastern and Himalayan 
states 
●  100% Central funding only for Union 
Territories without legislatures 
Therefore, the scheme is not fully funded by the 
Centre. Hence, Statement 3 is incorrect. 
 
4. Strengthened Social Audit Mechanism: To 
improve transparency and accountability, the 
Act mandates social audits at least once every 
six months. Gram Sabhas ar e assigned a 
stronger role in conducting these audits and 
ensuring public oversight of implementation.  
Hence, Statement 4 is correct.

subject: Environment & Ecology
question_text:
With reference to ballast water, which one 
of the following statements is correct?
option_a: It is seawater carried by ships to maintain stability and balance during voyages.
option_b: It is wastewater generated from ship engines and discharged into the sea.
option_c: It is a special fuel used by cargo vessels during long-distance navigation.
option_d: It refers to water stored exclusively in oil tankers for emergency firefighting purposes.
explanation:
maintain stability and balance during 
voyages. 
Explanation: 
 
Ballast water is water taken into special tanks 
by ships to maintain stability, balance, trim and 
structural integrity, particularly when carrying 
little or no cargo. The water is often taken in at 
one port and discharged at another when cargo 
is loaded. 
A major concern associated with ballast water is 
the introduction of invasive alien species into 
new ecosystems. Organisms present in ballast 
water may survive long voyages and establish 
themselves in non -native environments, 
threatening biodiversity, fisher ies and local 
livelihoods. 
A recent example is the proliferation of the 
Charru Mussel along parts of India's coastline. 
The Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department 
attributed the spread of this invasive mussel 
near Kamarajar Port to inadequate regulation of 
ballast water discharge from ships. The species 
has reportedly spread in water bodies such as 
Pulicat Lake and Ashtamudi Lake, where it 
competes with native species and affects fishing 
activities. 
This highlights why ballast water management 
is an importan t issue in marine conservation 
and maritime governance. Hence, option (a) is 
correct.

question_text:
With reference to 'cyber slavery', which 
one of the following statements is correct?
option_a: It refers to the exploitation of individuals who are trafficked or coerced into carrying out online scams, cyber frauds, or digital criminal activities against their will.
option_b: It refers to the excessive use of social media platforms leadi ng to internet addiction among youth.
option_c: It refers to the use of artificial intelligence systems to monitor employees in workplaces.
option_d: It refers to cyberattacks carried out by state - sponsored hacker groups against critical infrastructure.
explanation:
individuals who are trafficked or coerced 
into carrying out online scams, cyber frauds, 
or digital criminal activities against their 
will 
Explanation: 
Cyber slavery is an emerging form of human 
trafficking in which individua ls are lured with 
promises of lucrative overseas jobs and 
subsequently forced to work in scam 
compounds engaged in activities such as online 
fraud, cryptocurrency scams, romance scams, 
and phishing operations. 
Victims often have their passports confiscated , 
face physical abuse or threats, and are 
compelled to meet fraud targets under coercive 
conditions. Several such networks have been 
uncovered in parts of Southeast Asia, 
particularly in Myanmar, Cambodia, and Laos, 
where trafficked individuals are forced to 
participate in cyber-enabled crimes. 
The phenomenon represents a convergence of 
human trafficking, organised crime, cybercrime, 
and forced labour, making it a growing 
transnational security challenge. Hence, option 
(a) is correct.

subject: Polity & Governance
question_text:
With reference to the Prime Minister of 
India, consider the following statements: 
 
1. The Constitution prescribes a fixed tenure of 
five years for the Prime Minister. 
2. A person who is not a member of  either 
House of Parliament can be appointed as Prime 
Minister. 
3. The Prime Minister is the chairperson of the 
Council of Ministers and acts as the principal 
channel of communication between the 
President and the Council of Ministers. 
4. The Council of Minister s is collectively 
responsible to the Rajya Sabha. 
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
1. Tenure of the Prime Minister: The 
Constitution does not prescribe a fixed tenure 
for the Prime Minister. The Prime Minister 
remains in office as long as he or she enjoys the 
confidence of the Lok Sabha. Hence, Statement 
1 is incorrect. 
2. Membership of Parliament: A person who is 
not a member o f either House of Parliament can 
be appointed as Prime Minister, provided that 
he or she becomes a member of either House 
within six months. Hence, Statement 2 is 
correct. 
3. Head of the Council of Ministers: The Prime 
Minister is the head of the Council o f Ministers 
and serves as the principal channel of 
communication between the President and the 
Council of Ministers under Article 78. Hence, 
Statement 3 is correct. 
4. Collective Responsibility: Under Article 75(3), 
the Council of Ministers is collectively  
responsible to the Lok Sabha, not the Rajya 
Sabha. Hence, Statement 4 is incorrect. 
Additional Information 
As of June 2026, Narendra Modi has become the 
longest-serving elected Prime Minister of 
India in one continuous tenure , surpassing 
Jawaharlal Nehru' s uninterrupted tenure in 
office. However, the Constitution does not 
prescribe any maximum tenure or term limit for 
the office of the Prime Minister. A Prime 
Minister may continue in office as long as he or 
she commands the confidence of the Lok Sabha.

subject: International Relations
question_text:
With reference to the Group of Seven (G7), 
consider the following statements: 
 
1. The G7 is an informal grouping of advanced 
industrialised democracies. 
2. The G7 h as a permanent secretariat, and its 
decisions are legally binding on member 
countries. 
3. India is not a member of the G7 but has been 
invited to participate in several G7 summits as 
an outreach partner. 
4. The European Union participates in G7 
meetings but is n ot counted among the seven 
member countries. 
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
1. Nature of the G7: The G7 is an informal 
grouping of seven advanced economies that 
emerged in the 1970s in response to global 
economic challenges such as the oil crisis and 
financial instability. Unlike treaty -based 
international organizations, the G7 functions 
 
through consultations and consensus -building 
among member countries. 
 
Its members are: Canada, France, Germany, 
Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom, United States 
The forum discusses a wide range of issues 
including global economic governance, trade, 
energy security, climate change, internati onal 
security, technology, public health and 
development cooperation. Hence, Statement 1 
is correct. 
2. Institutional Structure and Decision-Making 
The G7 is not a formal international 
organization. It does not have: 
●  A founding treaty, 
●  A permanent headquarters, 
●  A permanent secretariat, 
●  Legally enforceable decisions. 
The presidency rotates annually among member 
countries, and the host country organizes the 
summit and sets the agenda for discussions. The 
declarations and communiqués issued after G7 
meetings r epresent political commitments and 
shared policy positions rather than legally 
binding obligations. This distinguishes the G7 
from organisations such as the World Trade 
Organization, whose agreements create legal 
obligations for members. Hence, Statement 2  
is incorrect. 
3. India's Participation in G7 Summits: India is 
not a member of the G7. Membership remains 
restricted to the seven advanced industrialized 
economies. 
However, India has emerged as a major global 
economic and strategic power and has therefor e 
been invited repeatedly as an outreach partner 
by successive G7 presidencies. India's 
participation allows discussions on: 
●  Global economic recovery, 
●  Climate action, 
●  Energy transition, 
●  Supply-chain resilience, 
●  Food security, 
●  Technology governance, 
●  Global South priorities. 
India's engagement with the G7 reflects its 
increasing role in shaping global governance 
despite not being a formal member. Hence, 
Statement 3 is correct. 
4. Participation of the European Union: The 
European Union participates in G7 meetings and 
is represented by the Presidents of the: 
●  European Commission 
●  European Council 
However, the EU is not counted among the 
seven members because the G7's name refers 
specifically to seven sovereign states. The EU 
therefore, enjoys a unique participator y status 
without formal membership.  Hence, Statement 
4 is correct.

subject: General Studies
question_text:
With reference to black holes, consider 
the following statements: 
 
1. A black hole is a region in space where 
gravity is so strong that even light cannot 
escape from it. 
2. Sagittarius A* is the supermassive black hole 
located at the centre of the Milky Way galaxy. 
3. Black holes can influence the formation and 
evolution of stars by interacting with 
surrounding gas and dust. 
4. Every black hole continuously absorbs all 
nearby matter and can never eject energy or 
material into space. 
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
1. Nature of a Black Hole 
 
A black hole is a region of spacetime where 
gravity is so intense that nothing, including 
light, can escape once it crosses the event 
horizon. Hence, Statement 1 is correct. 
2. Sagittarius A* 
 
Sagittarius A* is the supermassive black hole 
located at the centre of the Milky Way galaxy. It 
has a mass of about four million times that of 
the Sun. Hence, Statement 2 is correct. 
3. Role in Galactic Evolution 
Black holes can significantly influence their 
surroundings. Recent observations indicate that 
winds generated near Sagittarius A* can push 
away gas that would otherwise form stars. Such 
interactions affect star formation rates and the 
long-term evolution of galaxies. Hence, 
Statement 3 is correct. 
 
 
4. Ejection of Energy and Matter 
While matter crossing the event horizon cannot 
escape, the regions surrounding black holes can 
generate powerful jets and winds through 
processes occurring in the accretion disk. These 
outflows can eject enormous amounts of e nergy 
and matter into space.  Hence, Statement 4 is 
incorrect.  
Additional Information:  
The recent discovery of a cone -shaped outflow 
from Sagittarius A* using the Atacama Large 
Millimeter/submillimeter Array  in Chile 
provides strong evidence that the Milk y Way's 
central black hole is actively influencing its 
environment. Such black -hole-driven winds are 
important in regulating star formation and 
shaping the evolution of galaxies over cosmic 
timescales.

advanced AI systems possess the ability to 
autonomously identify, chain together, and 
exploit previously unknown software 
vulnerabilities at machine speed. Such 

 
capabilities could pose serious risks to critical 
infrastructure, financi al systems, power grids,

What are Zero-Day Vulnerabilities? 
A zero-day vulnerability  is a software flaw 
that is unknown to the software developer and  
for which no security patch exists. Attackers can 
exploit such vulnerabilities before they are 
detected and fixed.

faster than human experts.

targets.

India operates one of the world's largest digital

subject: Science & Technology
question_text:
With reference to Cholera, consider the 
following statements: 
 
1. Cholera is caused by a bacterium that 
spreads primarily through contaminated food 
and water. 
2. Severe cholera can lead to rapid dehydration 
and death if left untreated. 
3. Cholera is transmitted through mosquito 
bites. 
4. Improved sanitation and access to safe 
drinking water are key measures for preventing 
cholera outbreaks. 
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
1. Causative Agent: Cholera is an acute 
diarrhoeal disease caused by the bacterium 
Vibrio cholerae. Infection occurs mainly through 
the consumption of contaminated water or food. 
Hence, Statement 1 is correct. 
 
2. Health Impact:  Cholera can cause profuse 
watery diarrhoea and vomitin g, leading to 
severe dehydration. Without prompt treatment, 
the disease can be fatal within hours.  Hence, 
Statement 2 is correct. 
3. Mode of Transmission: Cholera is not 
transmitted by mosquitoes or other insect 
vectors. It spreads through the faecal -oral route, 
usually via contaminated food and water. 
Hence, Statement 3 is incorrect. 
4. Prevention: The most effective preventive 
measures include access to safe drinking water, 
proper sanitation, hygiene practices, and 

 
vaccination in high -risk areas. Hence, 
Statement 4 is correct. 
Additional Information 
●  Cholera remains a major public health 
challenge in regions with inadequate water and 
sanitation infrastructure. 
●  Symptoms include severe diarrhoea, 
vomiting, muscle cramps and dehydration. 
●  Oral Rehydration Solut ion (ORS) is the 
cornerstone of treatment. 
●  The World Health Organization  has 
identified cholera as a global public health 
threat, particularly in areas affected by conflict, 
displacement and natural disasters. 
●  Recent outbreaks have been reported in 
parts of Nigeria, highlighting the importance of 
water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) 
interventions.

subject: Science & Technology
question_text:
With reference to nuclear weapons and 
global nuclear arsenals, consider the 
following statements: 
 
1. The United States and Russia together 
possess the overwhelming majority of the 
world's nuclear warheads. 
2. China is currently reducing its nuclear 
arsenal in accordance with global disarmament 
commitments. 
3. Nuclear-armed states include India, Pakistan, 
Israel and North Korea. 
4. The number of nuclear warheads available 
for potential use has been increasing in recent 
years despite a long -term decline in total global 
stockpiles. 
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
1. Dominance of the U.S. and Russia: The United 
States and Russia together account for the vast 
majority of the world's nuclear weapons, 
possessing more than 80% of the global nuclear 
stockpile. Hence, Statement 1 is correct. 
2. China's Nuclear Expansion: China is not 
reducing its nuclear arsenal. Recent 
assessments indicate that it is expanding its 
nuclear capabilities and increasing the number 
of warheads in its inventory.  Hence, Statement 
2 is incorrect. 
3. Nuclear -Armed States: The nine nuclear -
armed states are: 
●  United States 
●  Russia 
●  China 
●  France 
●  United Kingdom 
●  India 
●  Pakistan 
●  Israel 
●  North Korea 
Hence, Statement 3 is correct. 
4. Stockpile vs Operational W arheads: Although 
the total number of nuclear warheads 
worldwide has generally declined since the Cold 
War, the number of warheads available for 
potential use or deployed on delivery systems 
has shown an increasing trend in recent years. 
Hence, Statement 4 is correct. 
Additional Information 
Nuclear Weapons and Artificial Intelligence 
A growing concern is the integration of Artificial 
Intelligence into nuclear command -and-control 
systems. Potential risks include: 
●  Faster escalation during crises. 
●  Misinterpretation of data by autonomous 
systems. 
●  Reduced human oversight in nuclear 
decision-making. 
●  Increased vulnerability to cyberattacks and 
misinformation. 
 
 
 
India's Nuclear Doctrine 
India follows: 
●  No First Use (NFU) policy. 
●  Credible Minimum Deterrence. 
●  Civilian political control over nuclear 
weapons. 
1. Treaty on the Non -Proliferation of Nuclear 
Weapons (NPT), 1968 
●  Aims to prevent the spread of nuclear 
weapons, promote peaceful uses of nuclear 
energy, and advance nuclear disarmament. 
●  Recognizes only five Nuclear Weapon States 
(U.S., Russia, U.K., France and China) based on 
their status before 1 January 1967. 
●  India is not a party to the NPT , as it 
considers the treaty discriminatory. 
2. Comprehensive Nuclear -Test-Ban Treaty 
(CTBT), 1996 
●  Prohibits all nuclear explos ions for military 
and civilian purposes. 
●  Has not entered into force globally because 
some key states have not ratified it. 
●  India is not a signatory to the CTBT , citing 
concerns over its discriminatory nature and lack 
of a time-bound commitment to disarmament. 
3. Partial Test Ban Treaty (PTBT), 1963 
●  Prohibits nuclear tests in the atmosphere, 
outer space and underwater. 
●  Permits underground nuclear testing. 
●  India is a party to the PTBT. 
4. Convention on the Physical Protection of 
Nuclear Material (CPPNM), 1980 
●  Seeks to ensure the physical protection of 
nuclear material during international transport 
and domestic use. 
●  India is a party to the CPPNM and its 2005 
Amendment. 
5. International Atomic Energy Agency 
(IAEA) Safeguards 
●  India has signed safeguards agreemen ts with 
the IAEA for its civilian nuclear facilities under 
the India -U.S. Civil Nuclear Agreement 
framework. 
●  India is a member of the IAEA. 
6. Convention on Nuclear Safety (CNS), 1994 
●  Promotes high standards of nuclear safety in 
civilian nuclear power plants. 
●  India is a party to the Convention on 
Nuclear Safety. 
7. Convention on Early Notification of a 
Nuclear Accident 
●  Requires states to promptly notify others of 
nuclear accidents with potential transboundary 
effects. 
●  India is a party. 
8. Convention on Assi stance in the Case of a 
Nuclear Accident or Radiological Emergency 
●  Facilitates international cooperation during 
nuclear emergencies. 
●  India is a party.

explanation:

Explanation

soda and chlorine 
Membrane Cell Technology (MCT) uses a 
selective membrane to separate products 
during the chlor -alkali process. It is considered 
more energy -efficient and environmentally 
friendly than the older mercury -cell process, 
which posed significant pollution risks.  Hence, 
Option (a) is correct.

for developing genetically modified crops

technology and has no connection with genetic 
modification of crops . Hence, Option (b) is 
incorrect.

system for water conservation in agriculture

Hence, Option (c) is incorrect.

hydrogen-powered vehicles

mobility technologies . Hence, Option (d) is 
incorrect.

Q. With reference to the International 
Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), consider the 
following statements: 
 
1. It is an aut onomous intergovernmental 
organization within the United Nations system 
headquartered in Vienna, Austria. 
2. The IAEA is responsible for enforcing 
compliance with the Nuclear Non -Proliferation 
Treaty (NPT) through sanctions against 
member states. 
3. The IAEA pro motes the peaceful use of 
nuclear technology and verifies that nuclear 
materials are not diverted for military purposes. 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct? 
 
(a) 1 and 2 only 
(b) 3 only 
(c) 1 and 3 only 
(d) 1, 2 and 3 
 
Answer: (c) 1 and 3 only 
Explanation 
Statement 1:  The International Atomic Energy 
Agency (IAEA) was established in 1957 and is 
an independent intergovernmental organization 
within the UN system. It is headquartered in 
Vienna, Austria. Hence, Statement 1 is correct. 
Statement 2:  The IAEA does not impose 
sanctions on countries. Its role is to inspect, 
verify, and report compliance regarding nuclear 
activities. Enforcement actions and sanctions, if 
required, are decided by bodies such as the UN 
Security Council.  Hence, Statement 2 is  
incorrect. 
Statement 3:  One of the core objectives of the 
IAEA is to promote the peaceful use of nuclear 
science and technology while ensuring, through 
safeguards and inspections, that nuclear 
materials are not diverted for nuclear weapons 
programmes. Hence, Statement 3 is correct.

subject: Polity & Governance
question_text:
With reference to the Tenth Schedule of 
the Constitution of India, co nsider the 
following statements: 
 
1. A member shall not be disqualified on 
grounds of defection if his political party merges 
with another political party and at least two -
thirds of the members of the legislature party 
agree to such merger. 
2. An independent mem ber elected to a House 
can join a political party after the election 
without attracting disqualification. 
3. The power to decide questions relating to 
disqualification under the Tenth Schedule rests 
with the Speaker or Chairman of the House. 
 
Which of the sta tements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
Statement 1:  Under the Tenth Schedule, 
disqualification on grounds of defection does 
not apply in case of a merger, provided  that at 
least two -thirds of the members of the 
legislature party agree to such merger.  Hence, 
Statement 1 is correct. 
Statement 2:  An independent member who 
joins any political party after being elected to 
the House is liable for disqualification under th e 
Anti-Defection Law. Hence, Statement 2 is 
incorrect. 
Statement 3: The authority to decide questions 
relating to disqualification under the Tenth 
Schedule is vested in the Speaker or Chairman 
of the House.Decision is subject to judicial 
review after Kihoto Hollohan (1992). Speaker's 
decision is not completely immune from judicial 
review. Hence, Statement 3 is correct.

Act, 1985

🔹 Purpose: Curb political defections and ensure 
stability of governments 
🔹 Exception: Merger supported by 2/3rd 
members of the legislature party

members

Defection Law.

question_text:
With reference to the Armed Forces 
(Special Powers) Act (AFSPA), consider the 
following statements: 
 
1. Under AFSPA, a region declared as a 
"disturbed area"  must be reviewed periodically 
and such a declaration cannot continue 
indefinitely without review. 
2. No prosecution, suit or other legal 
proceeding can be instituted against a person 
acting under AFSPA without the prior sanction 
of the Central Government. 
 
Which of the statements given above is/are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
Statement 1:  In Naga People's Movement of 
Human Rights v. Union of India, the Supreme 
Court upheld the const itutional validity of 
AFSPA and held that the declaration of a 
"disturbed area" should be reviewed 
periodically, generally every six months. Hence, 
Statement 1 is correct. 
Statement 2: Section 6 of AFSPA provides legal 
protection to armed forces personnel.  No 
prosecution, suit or other legal proceeding can 
be initiated against any person acting under the 
Act without the prior sanction of the Central 
Government. Hence, Statement 2 is correct. 
Value Addition 
●  AFSPA is not a Constitutional provision , 
but an ordinary Act of Parliament.

🔹 Objective: Assist civil authorities in 
maintaining public order in disturbed areas. 
🔹 Authority to Declare Disturbed Area: Central 
Government, Governor of a State, or 
Administrator of a Union Territory.

●  Arrest without warrant 
●  Search without warrant 
●  Use force, including lethal force, under 
specified conditions 
●  Destroy arms dumps and militant hideouts

With reference to the Shanghai

1. The SCO was established in 2001 in

3. The SCO evolved from the Shanghai Five 
mechanism. 
4. India and Pakistan became full members of 
the SCO in 2017. 
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
Statement 1: The Shanghai Cooperation 
Organisation (SCO) was formally established on 
15 June 2001  in Shanghai, China . The 
organisation was created to strengthen mutual 
trust, security cooperation, regional stability, 
and economic collaboration among member 
countries. Hence, Statement 1 is correct. 
Statement 2: The permanent Secretariat of 
the SCO is located in Beijing, China. It serves as 
the main administrative body responsible for 
coordinating activities among member states 
and implementing decisions of the SCO Council. 
Hence, Statement 2 is correct. 
Statement 3: The SCO originated from the 
Shanghai Five , a grouping formed in 1996 
consisting of China, Russia, Kazakhstan, 
Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan . Its primary 
objective was to resolve border disputes and 
enhance confidence-building measures after the 
dissolution of the Soviet Union. With the 
inclusion of Uzbekistan in 2001, the grouping 
evolved into the SCO.  Hence, Statement 3 is 
correct. 
 
Statement 4: India and Pakistan  were 
admitted as full members of the SCO during the 
Astana Summit (Kazakhstan) in 2017 , 
becoming the first countries outside the original 
Eurasian core to join the organisation  as full 
members. Hence, Statement 4 is correct.

subject: International Relations
question_text:
Consider the following statements: 
 
1. The United Nations General Assembly is one 
of the six principal organs of the United Nations. 
2. The General Assembly can amend the UN 
Charter through a simple majority vote. 
3. All member states of the Unit ed Nations are 
automatically members of the General 
Assembly. 
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
Statement 1: 
The United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) is 
one of the six principal organs of the United 
Nations established under the UN Charter. The 
six principal organs are: 
●  General Assembly 
●  Security Council 
●  Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) 
●  International Court of Justice (ICJ) 
●  Trusteeship Council 
●  Secretariat. Hence, Statement 1 is correct. 
Statement 2: 
Amendment of the UN Charter cannot be done 
through a simple majority vote in the General 
Assembly. Under Article 108 of the UN Charter, 
amendments require: 
●  A two -thirds majority vote in the  General 
Assembly, and 
●  Ratification by two -thirds of UN Member 
States, including all five permanent members of 
the Security Council . Hence, Statement 2 is 
incorrect. 
Statement 3: 
The General Assembly comprises all Member 
States of the United Nations. There fore, every 
country that is admitted as a UN member 
automatically becomes a member of the UN 
General Assembly with one vote each . Hence, 
Statement 3 is correct.

Consider the following statements 
regarding the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle 
(PSLV): 
 
1. It is a four-stage launch vehicle developed by 
ISRO. 
2. PSLV employs both solid and liqui d 
propulsion stages  
3. It is primarily used for placing satellites into 
Polar and Sun-Synchronous Orbits. 
4. It is capable of launching multiple satellites 
in a single mission. 
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
Statement 1:  PSLV is a four -stage launch 
vehicle developed by ISRO and is regarded as 
the workhorse of India's space programme.  
Hence, Statement 1 is correct. 
 
Statement 2: PSLV uses an alternating 
combination of solid and liquid propulsion 
systems, which provides both high thrust and 
precise control during flight. 
●  First Stage (PS1):  Solid propellant (HTPB -
based fuel) along with optional solid strap -on 
boosters. 
●  Second Stage (PS2 ): Liquid propellant stage 
powered by the Vikas engine , using UH25 fuel 
and N₂O₄ oxidizer. 
●  Third Stage (PS3): Solid propellant stage. 
●  Fourth Stage (PS4):  Liquid propellant stage 
using MMH fuel and MON oxidizer. 
This solid-liquid-solid-liquid configuration  
combines the advantages of: 
●  Solid propulsion:  High thrust and 
simplicity. 
●  Liquid propulsion:  Better control, restart 
capability (in PS4), and orbital precision. Hence, 
Statement 2 is correct. 
Statement 3:  PSLV was primarily designed for 
launching satellites  into Polar Orbits and Sun -
Synchronous Polar Orbits (SSPO), though it is 
also used for other missions. Hence, Statement 
3 is correct. 
Statement 4:  PSLV has demonstrated the 
capability to deploy multiple satellites in a 
single mission, including the record launch of 
104 satellites in 2017.  Hence, Statement 4 is 
correct.

Consider the following statements 
regarding Shigellosis: 
 
1. Shigellosis is caused by a bacterium and is 
primarily transmitted through the faeco -oral 
route. 
2. Humans are the only natural reservoir of the 
Shigella bacteria. 
3. The disease is transmitted exclusively 
through contaminated water and cannot spread 
through direct person-to-person contact. 
 
Which of the stateme nts given above are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
Statement 1: Shigellosis (bacillary dysentery) is 
a highly contagious diarrhoeal disease caused 
by Shigella bacteria. It c ommonly spreads 
through the faeco -oral route via contaminated 
food, water, or hands.  Hence, Statement 1 is 
correct. 
Statement 2:  Humans are considered the only 
natural reservoir of Shigella. The bacteria 
primarily survive and multiply in the human 
intestinal tract. Hence, Statement 2 is correct. 
Statement 3:  Shigellosis can spread through 
direct person -to-person contact, contaminated 
food and water, poor hygiene, and even certain 
sexual practices. Therefore, it is not transmitted 
exclusively through contami nated water . 
Hence, Statement 3 is incorrect.

negative bacillus)

food/water, direct contact 
🔹 Natural Reservoir: Humans 
 
🔹 High-Risk Groups: Children under 5 years, 
elderly, immunocompromised persons 
🔹Major Symptoms: Bloody diarrhoea,

🔹Concern: Rising antimicrobial resistance

Statement 1:  Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) 
occurs when microorganisms such as bacteria ,

and no longer respond to medicines used to 
treat infections. As a result, infections become 
harder to treat and the risk of disease spread, 
severe illness and death increases. Hence, 
Statement 1 is correct.

irrational use of antimicrobial medicines creates 
selective pressure on microbes, allowing 
resistant strains to survive and multiply. This is 
one of the major causes behind the emergence 
and spread of AMR globally. Hence, Statement 
2 is correct. 
Statement 3:  India launched the National 
Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance 
(NAP-AMR) in 2017. The National Centre for 
Disease Control (NCDC), New Delhi , serves as 
the focal point for implementation and 
coordination of t he action plan at the national 
level. Hence, Statement 3 is correct.

question_text:
Recent research on the Chocolate -chip Sea 
Star ( Protoreaster nodosus ) revealed a 
unique feature. What is it?
option_a: Ability to regenerate an entire body from a single cell
option_b: Presence of cone -shaped skeletal structures that gather and concentrate light
option_c: Capacity to survive in both marine and freshwater habitats
option_d: Production of electric fields for navigation
explanation:
skeletal structures that gather and 
concentrate light 
Explanation: 
1.  Sea stars  can regenerate lost arms and, in 
some species, portions of the body, but they 
cannot regenerate an entire organism from a 
single cell.Hence, Option (a) is incorrect. 
2.  Recent research has shown that the 
Chocolate-chip Sea Star ( Protoreaster 
nodosus) possesses cone-shaped skeletal 
structures at the tip of each arm that function 
similarly to optical fibres. These structures can 
transmit about 70% of incident light , 
concentrate it nearly three times at the base , 
and collectively brighten light inside the arm b y 
about eight times .Hence, option (b) is 
correct. 
3. Protoreaster nodosus  is a marine 
echinoderm found in tropical Indo -Pacific 
waters and does not inhabit freshwater 
environments.Hence, Option (c) is incorrect. 
4. The species is not known to produce electric 
fields for navigation ; this trait is associated 
with certain fishes such as electric rays and 
electric eels.Hence,Option (d) is incorrect.

question_text:
With reference to the Inner Line Permit 
(ILP) syste m, consider the following 
statements: 
 
1. The Inner Line Permit system traces its 
origin to the Bengal Eastern Frontier 
Regulation, 1873. 
2. At present, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, 
Mizoram and Manipur are covered under the 
ILP regime. 
3. The ILP is mandatory for both Indian citizens 
and foreign nationals visiting these states. 
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
Statement 1:  The ILP system originat ed from 
the Bengal Eastern Frontier Regulation, 
1873, enacted during British rule to regulate 
the movement of outsiders into tribal areas. 
Hence, Statement 1 is correct. 
Statement 2:  Currently, the ILP system is 
applicable in Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, 
Mizoram and Manipur. Hence, Statement 2 is 
correct. 
Statement 3:  ILP is meant for Indian citizens  
visiting notified areas. Foreign nationals require 
a Protected Area Permit (PAP)  wherever 
applicable, not an ILP.  Hence, Statement 3 is 
incorrect. 
Value Addition

●  Travel document for Indian citizens visiting 
protected tribal areas. 
●  Issued by the respective state governments. 
●  Objective: Protect indigenous communities, 
culture, customs, and land rights.

●  Closely ass ociated with tribal protection in 
the North-East. 
●  Complements safeguards under the Sixth 
Schedule and Article 371 provisions.

subject: General Studies
question_text:
Consider the foll owing statements 
regarding earthquakes: 
 
1. Earthquake tremors are caused by the 
sudden release of energy accumulated in rocks. 
2. Tremors propagate through the Earth in the 
form of seismic waves. 
3. Foreshocks are smaller tremors that may 
precede a major earthquake. 
4. India is presently divided into four seismic 
zones, Zones II - V. 
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
Statement 1: Earthquake tremors occur due to 
the sudden release of energy accumulated in 
rocks within the Earth's crust. This release 
generally takes place along faults where tectonic 
stresses have built up over time.  Hence, 
Statement 1 is correct. 
Statement 2:  The energy relea sed during an 
earthquake travels through the Earth in the 
 
form of seismic waves. These include Primary 
(P) waves, Secondary (S) waves and Surface 
waves. Hence, Statement 2 is correct. 
Statement 3:  Foreshocks are smaller 
earthquakes or tremors that may occu r before a 
larger earthquake (mainshock). However, not 
every major earthquake is preceded by 
foreshocks. Hence, Statement 3 is correct. 
Statement 4: According to the Bureau of Indian 
Standards (BIS), India is presently divided into 
four seismic zones --Zone II, Zone III, Zone IV 
and Zone V( representing the highest seismic 
risk) . Zone I was removed from the seismic 
zoning map in the revised classification.  Hence, 
Statement 4 is correct. 
Value Addition 
🔹 Foreshock: Smaller tremor occurring before 
the main earthquake. 
🔹 Mainshock: The largest earthquake in a 
seismic sequence. 
🔹 Aftershock: Smaller earthquakes occurring 
after the mainshock due to crustal 
readjustment. 
🔹 Seismic Zones of India: 
●  Zone II - Low Damage Risk 
●  Zone III - Moderate Damage Risk 
●  Zone IV - High Damage Risk 
●  Zone V - Very High Damage Risk 
🔹 About 59% of India's land area  is 
vulnerable to moderate to severe earthquake 
risk.

question_text:
With reference to Drop Shipping, consider 
the following statements: 
 
1. In drop shipping, the seller need not 
maintain inventory of the products being sold. 
2. The product is usually shipped directly from 
the manufacturer or wholesaler to the  
customer. 
 
Which of the statements given above is/are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
Statement 1:  In the drop shipping business 
model, the seller acts as an intermediary and 
does no t purchase or store inventory 
beforehand. Orders are forwarded to a third -
party supplier after a customer places an order.  
Hence, Statement 1 is correct. 
Statement 2: The manufacturer, wholesaler, or 
supplier fulfills the order and ships the product 
directly to the customer, while the drop shipper 
facilitates the transaction . Hence, Statement 2 
is correct. 
Value Addition 
🔹 Drop Shipping: An e -commerce model where 
the seller markets products without maintaining 
inventory. 
🔹 Key Advantage: Low startup costs due to the 
absence of warehousing and inventory 
management. 
🔹 Major Risks: Counterfeit products, delayed 
deliveries, poor quality control, and lack of 
transparency in the supply chain.

subject: Science & Technology
question_text:
In the context of dengue, the term 
"Antibody-Dependent Enhancement (ADE)" 
refers to
option_a: a process in which antibodies completely protect the body from all dengue infections
option_b: a phenomenon in which existing antibodies help the dengue virus infect cells more effectively, leading to severe disease
option_c: the weakening of the dengue v irus before it is used in a vaccine
option_d: the mutation of the dengue virus into a new serotype
explanation:
antibodies help the dengue virus infect cells 
more effectively, leading to severe disease 
Explanation 
Option (a): ADE do es not refer to complete 
protection against dengue infection. Instead, it 
occurs when antibodies fail to fully neutralise 
the virus. Hence, Option (a) is incorrect. 
Option (b):  Antibody-Dependent Enhancement 
(ADE) is a phenomenon in which antibodies 
from a previous dengue infection or vaccination 
do not completely neutralise the virus. Instead, 
they facilitate viral entry into immune cells, 
leading to increased viral replication and a 
higher risk of severe dengue. Hence, Option (b) 
is correct. 
Option (c):  The weakening of a virus for 
vaccine development is known as attenuation 
and is unrelated to ADE . Hence, Option (c) is 
incorrect. 
Option (d):  ADE is associated with the body's 
immune response and not with genetic 
mutation or the emergence of new dengue 
serotypes. Hence, Option (d) is incorrect. 
Value Addition 
🔹 Cause: Presence of non -neutralising or sub -
neutralising antibodies. 
🔹 Outcome: Increased viral multiplication and 
greater disease severity. 
🔹 ADE is one reason why a second dengue 
infection with a different serotype can be more 
severe. 
🔹 It may lead to serious conditions such as 
Dengue Haemorrhagic Fever (DHF) and Dengue 
Shock Syndrome (DSS). 
🔹 Significance: ADE is a major safety concern in 
the development and evaluation of dengue 
vaccines.

question_text:
With reference to the dengue vaccine 
DengiAll, consider the following statements: 
 
1. It is a live attenuated tetravalent dengue 
vaccine. 
2. It is being developed by Panacea  Biotec in 
collaboration with the Indian Council of Medical 
Research (ICMR). 
3. It is designed to provide protection against 
all four dengue virus serotypes. 
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
Statement 1:  DengiAll is a live attenuated 
tetravalent dengue vaccine  developed using 
weakened forms of the dengue virus. It contains 
components targeting all four dengue virus 
serotypes while being desig ned not to cause 
disease. Hence, Statement 1 is correct. 
Statement 2:  DengiAll is being developed by 
Panacea Biotec  in collaboration with the 
Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) . 
Its Phase III clinical trials are being conducted at 
multiple centres a cross India to assess safety 
and efficacy. Hence, Statement 2 is correct. 
Statement 3:  Dengue virus exists in four 
serotypes(a distinct variation of a 
microorganism identified by its surface 
antigens)--DENV-1, DENV -2, DENV -3, and 
DENV-4. DengiAll is a tetravalent vaccine , 
meaning it is designed to provide protection 
against all four serotypes and reduce the risk of 
dengue infection and severe disease.  Hence, 
Statement 3 is correct. 
Value Addition 
🔹 DengiAll: India's indigenous dengue vaccine 
candidate. 
 
🔹 Target: Protection against all four dengue 
virus serotypes (DENV -1, DENV -2, DENV -3 and 
DENV-4). 
🔹 Significance: If approved, it could become 
India's first indigenous vaccine for broad 
protection against dengue.

147. United Nations Convention on the 
Law of the Sea(UNCLOS) 
Q.With reference to maritime zones under 
UNCLOS, consider the following statements: 
 
1. Internal Water s lie on the landward side of 
the baseline and are under the full sovereignty 
of the coastal state. 
2. Foreign vessels enjoy the right of innocent 
passage through Territorial Waters up to 12 
nautical miles from the baseline. 
3. The Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) extends 
up to 200 nautical miles from the baseline, 
where the coastal state has exclusive rights over 
natural resources. 
4. The Continental Shelf grants the coastal state 
exclusive rights over both the seabed resources 
and the water column above it. 
 
Which of  the statements given above are 
correct? 
 
(a) 1, 2 and 3 only 
(b) 1 and 4 only 
(c) 2, 3 and 4 only 
(d) 1, 2, 3 and 4 
 
Answer: (a) 1, 2 and 3 only 
Explanation 
Statement 1:  Internal Waters are the waters 
located on the landward side of the baseline. 
The coas tal state exercises complete 
sovereignty over these waters, similar to its 
land territory. Hence, Statement 1 is correct. 
Statement 2:  Territorial Waters extend up to 
12 nautical miles from the baseline. Foreign 
ships are allowed innocent passage, provided  
their passage is continuous and not prejudicial 
to the peace, order, or security of the coastal 
state. Hence, Statement 2 is correct. 
Statement 3:  The Exclusive Economic Zone 
(EEZ) extends up to 200 nautical miles from the 
baseline. Within the EEZ, the co astal state 
enjoys sovereign rights for exploring, exploiting, 
conserving, and managing natural resources.  
Hence, Statement 3 is correct. 
Statement 4: The Continental Shelf grants 
rights only over the seabed and subsoil 
resources such as oil, natural gas, and minerals. 
It does not confer rights over the water column 
above it. Hence, Statement 4 is incorrect. 
Value Addition 
🔹 Baseline: Usually the low-water line along the 
coast from which maritime zones are measured. 
🔹 Territorial Sea: Up to 12 nautical miles. 
🔹 Contiguous Zone: Up to 24 nautical miles 
from the baseline. 
🔹 EEZ: Up to 200 nautical miles from the 
baseline. 
🔹 High Seas: Beyond national jurisdiction; open 
to all states. 
🔹 Right of Innocent Passage: Available through 
Territorial Waters but not through Internal 
Waters.

subject: Economy
question_text:
Consider t he following statements 
regarding an Initial Public Offering (IPO): 
 
1. An IPO is the process through which a 
company offers its shares to the public for the 
first time. 

 
2. In an Offer for Sale (OFS), the company 
receives the entire proceeds from the issue. 
3. SEBI determines the final issue price of an 
IPO under the book-building process. 
4. After an IPO, the company's shares can be 
traded on a stock exchange. 
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
Statement 1:  An Initial Public Offering (IPO) is 
the process through which a private company 
offers its shares to the public for the first time 
and becomes a publicly listed company. Hence, 
Statement 1 is correct. 
Statement 2: In an Offer for Sale (OFS), existing 
shareholders such as promoters, investors, or 
the government sell their shares to the public. 
The proceeds go to the selling shareholders and 
not to the company.  Hence, Statement 2 is 
incorrect. 
Statement 3: SEBI does not determine the price 
of an IPO. Under the book -building process, the 
issue price is discovered based on investor 
demand within the prescribed price band. 
SEBI's role is to ensure transparency and 
investor protection.  Hence, St atement 3 is 
incorrect. 
Statement 4: After successful completion of the 
IPO and listing process, the company's shares 
are traded on recognised stock exchanges such 
as the National Stock Exchange and the Bombay 
Stock Exchange. Hence, Statement 4 is correct. 
Value Addition

into a publicly listed company.

Consider the f ollowing statements 
regarding the Sustainable Harnessing and 
Advancement of Nuclear Energy for 
Transforming India (SHANTI) Act, 2025: 
 
1. It replaces the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and 
the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010. 
2. It allows private companies  and foreign 
entities to build and operate nuclear power 
plants in India. 
3. It retains supplier liability for nuclear 
accidents under the existing framework. 
4. It grants statutory status to the Atomic 
Energy Regulatory Board (AERB). 
 
Which of the statements gi ven above are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
Statement 1: The SHANTI Act, 2025 establishes 
a unified legal framework by replacing the 
Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and  the Civil Liability 
for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010.  Hence, 
Statement 1 is correct. 
Statement 2:  The Act opens India's nuclear 
sector to private participation by allowing 
private companies, joint ventures, and foreign 
 
entities to build, own, operate, and 
decommission nuclear power plants. Hence, 
Statement 2 is correct. 
Statement 3:  One of the major reforms under 
the Act is the removal of supplier liability. The 
operator of the nuclear plant is solely 
responsible for compensation in the event of 
nuclear damage . Hence, Statement 3 is 
incorrect. 
Statement 4: The Act grants statutory status to 
the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB), 
strengthening regulatory independence, 
oversight, and accountability . Hence, 
Statement 4 is correct. 
Value Addition

about 8 GW to 100 GW by 2047. 
🔹 Key Reform: Ends the monopoly of the 
Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited in 
nuclear power generation.

retained; supplier liability removed.

Modular Reactors (SMRs) and advanced nuclear 
technologies.

achieving net-zero emissions by 2070.

question_text:
With reference to the United Nations 
Security Council (UNSC), consider the 
following statements: 
 
1. The UNSC consists of 15 members, including 
5 permanent members with veto power. 
2. Non-permanent members of the UNSC are 
elected by the UN General Assembly for a term 
of three years. 
 
Which of the statements given above is/are 
correct?
explanation:
Statement 1: The United Nations Security 
Council (UNSC) consists of 15 members --5 
permanent members (China, France, Russia, 
the United Kingdom, and the United States)  
and 10 non -permanent members . The 
permanent members enjoy veto power. Hence, 
Statement 1 is correct. 
Statement 2: The 10 non -permanent 
members are elected by the UN General 
Assembly for a two-year term , not a three -
year term. Hence, Statement 2 is incorrect. 
Additional Information 
●  The UNSC is one of the five principal organs 
of the United Nations. 
●  It has the primary responsibility for 
maintaining international peace and 
security. 
●  Under the UN Charter, all member states are 
required to comply with UNSC decisions. 
●  The UNSC  is headquartered at the United 
Nations Headquarters in New York City.

subject: Environment & Ecology
question_text:
Which of the following National Parks is 
known as the world's only known  natural 
habitat of wild melanistic tigers?
explanation:
Option (a) : Bhitarkanika National Park is 
famous for its mangrove ecosystem, estuarine 
crocodiles, and rich coastal biodiversity. It is not 
known for melanistic tigers. 
Option (b): Similipal National Park is the 
world's only known natural habitat of wild 
 
melanistic (black) tigers. It is located in Odish a's 
Mayurbhanj district and forms part of the 
Similipal Tiger Reserve. The park is also known 
for its sal forests, rich biodiversity, waterfalls 
such as Barehipani and Joranda, and a 
significant population of Royal Bengal Tigers 
and elephants. Hence, Option (b) is correct. 
 
Option (c) :Satkosia National Park is known for 
the Satkosia Gorge formed by the Mahanadi 
River and its tiger and crocodile conservation 
efforts. It is not associated with melanistic 
tigers. 
Option (d): Bandipur National Park is an 
important tiger reserve in southern India and 
part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, but it is 
not known as the natural habitat of wild 
melanistic tigers. Hence, Option (d) is 
incorrect 
Additional Information 
●  Similipal was recently declared Odisha's 
second National Park after Bhitarkanika. 
●  It became the 107th National Park of India. 
●  The park falls under the Deccan Peninsular 
Biogeographic Zone, Chhotanagpur Province, 
and the Mahanadian Region. 
●  It is home to around 40 Royal Bengal Tigers 
presently, including the unique melanistic 
population. 
●  Major ungulates found here include sambar, 
chital, barking deer, gaur, and mouse deer. 
●  The reserve supports nearly 25% of Odisha's 
elephant population and more than 100 species 
of orchids. 
●  Similipal is also recognised as a fla gship 
landscape for tiger and elephant conservation in 
eastern India.

than Natural World Heritage Sites. 
 
Which of the statements given  above are

Statement 1: UNESCO was established in 1945 
as a specialised agency of the United Nations. It 
promotes international cooperation in the fields 
of education, science, culture and 
communication, and administers the World 
Heritage Convention . Hence, Statement 1 is 
correct. 
Statement 2:  Khangchendzonga National Park 
is India's only Mixed World Heritage Site, 
inscribed by UNESCO in 2016. It  was recognised 
for both its exceptional natural features, 
including Eastern Himalayan biodiversity, and 
its cultural significance linked to indigenous 
Sikkimese traditions and sacred landscapes . 
Hence, Statement 2 is correct. 
Statement 3:  India has 44 UNE SCO World 
Heritage Sites (as of February 2026), 
comprising 36 Cultural Sites, 7 Natural Sites and 
1 Mixed Site. Since the number of Cultural Sites 
is significantly higher than the number of 
Natural Sites, India has more Cultural World 

 
Heritage Sites than N atural World Heritage 
Sites. Hence, Statement 3 is correct.

subject: International Relations
question_text:
With reference to the Group of Twenty 
(G20), consider the following statements: 
 
1. The G20 is an informal forum for 
international economic cooperation. 
2. The G20 comprises 19 countries, the 
European Union and the African Union. 
3. The Troika consists of the previous, current 
and next G20 Presidencies. 
4. Decisions of the G20 are generally based on 
consensus. 
 
Which of the statements given  above are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
Statement 1: The G20 (Group of Twenty) is an 
informal forum for international economic 
cooperation that brings together m ajor 
developed and developing economies to discuss 
global economic, financial, and development 
issues. It does not function as a treaty -based 
international organisation. Hence, Statement 1 
is correct. 
Statement 2:  The G20 currently comprises 19 
individual countries, the European Union (EU), 
and the African Union (AU), which became a 
permanent member during the 2023 G20 
Summit hosted by India. Hence, Statement 2 is 
correct. 
Statement 3: The Troika is the G20's continuity 
mechanism and consists of the previou s, 
current, and incoming Presidencies. It helps 
ensure consistency in the G20 agenda and 
priorities across successive presidencies.  
Hence, Statement 3 is correct. 
Statement 4:  The G20 does not have a formal 
voting mechanism. Its declarations, 
communiqués, and policy outcomes are 
generally adopted through consensus among 
members, making cooperation and negotiation 
central to its functioning. Hence, Statement 4 
is correct. 
About G20 
●  Established in 1999 after the Asian Financial 
Crisis. 
●  Initially, a meeting of  Finance Ministers and 
Central Bank Governors. 
●  Elevated to the Leaders' Summit level in 
2008 following the Global Financial Crisis. 
●  Represents around: 
○ 85% of global GDP 
○ 75% of international trade 
○ Two-thirds of the world's population 
●  Permanent Secretariat: None (the presidency 
rotates annually). 
●  Headquarters: None. 
●  Presidency rotates among members grouped 
into regional categories. 
Objectives of G20 
●  Promote global economic stability and 
sustainable growth. 
●  Strengthen the international financial 
architecture. 
●  Address issues such as climate change, 
energy security, food security, health, digital 
transformation, and sustainable development. 
●  Enhance cooperation between developed 
and developing economies. 
Members of the G20 
Countries: Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, 
China, France, Germany, India, Indonesia, Italy, 
Japan, Mexico, Republic of Korea, Russia, Saudi 
Arabia, South Africa, Türkiye, United Kingdom, 
United States. 
Regional Organisations: 
●  European Union 
●  African Union 
Troika Example 
For the G20 South Afr ica Presidency (2025), the 
Troika consists of: 
●  Brazil (Previous) 
 
●  South Africa (Current) 
●  United States (Incoming) 
This arrangement ensures continuity and 
smooth transition of priorities across 
presidencies.

subject: International Relations
question_text:
With reference to Geographical 
Indications (GI) in India, consider the 
following statements: 
 
1. A Geographical Indication (GI) tag is granted 
to products whose quality, reputation or 
characteristics are essentially  attributable to a 
specific geographical origin. 
2. The registration and protection of GI tags in 
India are governed by the Geographical 
Indications of Goods (Registration and 
Protection) Act, 1999. 
3. Bhagaiya Silk, Kuchai Silk, Munda Jewellery 
and Jharkhand Ba mboo Craft recently received 
GI tags from Jharkhand. 
 
Which of the statements given above are 
correct?
explanation:
Explanation 
Statement 1:  A Geographical Indication (GI)  
is a s ign used on products that have a specific 
geographical origin  and possess qualities, 
reputation, or characteristics that are 
essentially attributable to that place of origin. GI 
tags help distinguish products that derive their 
uniqueness from local natural  factors, 
traditional skills, or cultural heritage. Hence, 
Statement 1 is correct. 
Statement 2:  Geographical Indications are 
recognised as a form of Intellectual Property 
Right (IPR)  under the Agreement on Trade -
Related Aspects of Intellectual Property 
Rights (TRIPS)  of the World Trade 
Organization (WTO). In India, GI protection is 
provided under the Geographical Indications 
of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 
1999. A registered GI grants collective rights to 
authorised producers of a region and pro tects 
the product from misuse or imitation by 
unauthorised persons . Hence, Statement 2 is 
correct. 
Statement 3:  Recently, four traditional 
products from Jharkhand received GI tags: 
●  Bhagaiya Silk  - Traditional hand -spun silk 
textile of the Santhal Pargana r egion, known for 
tribal motifs and indigenous weaving 
techniques. 
●  Kuchai Silk - Produced in Kuchai (Saraikela-
Kharsawan district) from Tasar (Tussar) silk 
and famous for its natural golden sheen and 
durability. 
●  Munda Jewellery  - Traditional jewellery of 
the Munda tribe made from silver, brass and 
beads, reflecting tribal identity and culture. 
●  Jharkhand Bamboo Craft  - Traditional 
bamboo handicrafts produced by tribal and 
rural artisans, supporting sustainable 
livelihoods.Hence, Statement 3 is correct. 
About Geographical Indications (GI) 
●  A GI tag identifies products whose quality, 
reputation, or other characteristics  are 
linked to a particular geographical area. 
●  It is a form of collective intellectual 
property right , benefiting communities rather 
than individual producers. 
●  GI registration is administered by the GI 
Registry, Chennai , under the Department for 
Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade 
(DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry. 
●  Registration is valid for 10 years and can be 
renewed indefinitely. 
●  Unlike patents, a GI does not grant exclusive 
rights to a single inventor; instead, it protects 
the collective rights of producers belonging to a 
specific geographical region.  
●  GI tags can be granted to: 
○ Agricultural products 
○ Handicrafts 
 
○ Food products 
○ Textiles 
○ Industrial products 
○ Wines and spirits 
Benefits of GI Tags 
●  Provides legal protection against 
unauthorised use. 
●  Enhances market value and global 
recognition of local products. 
●  Preserves traditional knowledge and cultural 
heritage. 
●  Promotes rural livelihood s and local 
economic development. 
●  Prevents misappropriation and imitation of 
region-specific products. 
Important International Frameworks 
●  Paris Convention (1883)  - Recognises 
protection of industrial property, including 
geographical indications. 
●  TRIPS Agre ement (1995)  - Provides 
international legal protection for GIs under the 
WTO framework. 
●  Lisbon Agreement (1958)  - Facilitates 
international protection of appellations of 
origin. 
●  Madrid System  - Primarily for trademarks 
but can indirectly aid GI protection through 
collective or certification marks.
